7. At the time of hearing of the revision, it appears that the Lower Court Record is not available. In such circumstances, opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed an application for calling of the Lower Court Record. Accordingly this court allowed the said application by order dated 8-12-2016 and directed the learned Joint District Judge, Artha Rin Adalat-4, Dhaka and Senior Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka to sent the Lower Court Record of Title Appeal No. 623 of 1999 and Title Suit No. 3 of 1991 within two weeks from the date of receipt of the order. 

 8. In compliance of the said order, two files LCR of Title Appeal No. 623 of 1999 was sent to this court by memo dated 5-1-2017. After scrutiny of the case record, section reported that except SA Khatian (Exhibit-2) all other Exhibits Nos.1-3 to 14(Ka) are available in the case record, but the record of the Title Suit No. 3 of 1991was not sent to this court. Subsequently, another notice was sent by the office to transmit the record of Senior Assistant Judge, Third Court, Dhaka of Title Suit No. 3 of 1991. Thereafter, Senior Assistant Judge, Third Court, Dhaka, by memo dated 9-1-2017 informed that the LCR of Title Suit No. 3 of 1991 has been destroyed in the year 2015 as such could not send the Lower Court Record. 

 9. In such circumstances, when the record has been destroyed defendant No.1 as substituted heir of defendant-opposite party No.2 was compelled to file an application on 14-5-2017 under Section 151 for reconstruction of the file for missing Exhibits of the defendants along with photostate copies of those missing Exhibit Nos. Ka-Cha. The matter was appeared in the daily cause list on 24-8-2017 but the hearing of the application was adjourned till 23-11-2017. Subsequently, on 23-5-2018 petitioners filed supplementary-affidavit by taking some new grounds in the present revisional application. 

 10. Against the supplementary-affidavit of the petitioners dated 23-5-2018, the defendant-opposite party Nos.1 and 2 filed supplementary-affidavit on 27-5-2018 stating that section 94(e) of the Code of Civil Procedure contemplates that in order to prevent the ends of justice from being defeated the court may, if it is so prescribed make such other interlocutory orders as may appear to the court to be just and convenient. Since the petitioner in his supplementary-affidavit dated 23-5-2018 stated that only trial court reconsidered the case record as per Civil Rules and Order. On 16-11-2017 opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed another supplementary-affidavit that stating defendants missing Exhibits were destroyed when the case record was sent from the High Court Division to the trial court. The opposite party No.2 after much effort able to collect certified copies of Exhibit-"Ka-"Ga' and "Uma' and "Cha 'and photocopy of the Exhibit-Ga but failed to submit Exhibit-1' and submitted those Exhibits by list of documents with the supplementary-affidavit, which is described below: 

 11. It appears that Exhibit-'Ga' is the original registered Sale Deed No. 9400 dated 21-4-1985 executed by Keshob Lal son of late Radhu Mistry and Ahladi Bewa wife of late Ishar Mali of Dhonia, Demra, in favour of Ali Akbor, Samsul Haque son of late Akram Khan of Donia, Police Station-Demra, Dhaka. The certified copy of the said sale deed dated 21-4-1985 was produced by the plaintiffs-petitioners in the trial which was also marked as Exhibit-9. Subsequently, on 26-7-2018 learned Advocate for the petitioner filed photocopy of the original Sale Deed dated 21-4-1985 marked in the Tile Suit No 3 of 1991on 18-7-1999 as (Exhibit-Ga) filed before this court along with the photocopy of SA Khatian (Exhibit-2) which was missing from the LCR and accordingly same was kept with the record. Since both contesting parties agreed that the exhibited documents filed by the defendant-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 on 16-11-2017 are the same document which was marked in the suit as Exhibit No. 2 and `Ga' respectively. The two documents are kabala dated 21-4-1985 (Exhibit-Ga) and SA khatian (Exhibit-2) which was subsequently filed by the plaintiff petitioner before this court on 26-11-2017. Since all this documents were reconstructed by the learned advocate of both the parties and they have no objection for such reconstruction. Accordingly, the missing documents Exhibit Nos. Ka-Cha filed by the defendants and Exhibit-ga and Exhibit-2 is reconstructed. The above reconstructed Exhibited documents be kept with the record under separate list of documents prepared by this court on 21-1-2019 Accordingly the application for reconstruction of missing Exhibited documents filed by the opposite party is allowed. The list of reconstructed Exhibited document prepared by this court on 21-1-2019 kept with the record. 

 13. It may be noted that although the matter was sent from the Appellate Division to hear and dispose of the same within a period of two months from the date of receipt of the judgment. After receipt of Judgment from the Appellate Division the matter was posted in the daily cause list for hearing. As we have already stated that due to the destruction of the exhibited documents of the defendant Nos. I and 2 by the trial court, matter could not be heard for last three and half years. Since record was reconstructed in respect of the exhibited documents of the defendants, which were marked as Exhibit-ka-cha, now we have taken to dispose of this civil revision. 

 15. The positive case of the plaintiff, is that, the suit land belonged to Ahladi Bewa and CS record was prepared in her name and she died leaving only son Shamboo Nath who died leaving wife Sreemoti Bewa; that Sreemoti Bewa by kabala dated 28-4-1952 sold the land that she got from Shamboo Nath to Khetro Mohan Baroi; that Khetro Mohan Baroi entered into an oral agreement on 14-8-1961 with the plaintiff for selling the land and upon receiving Taka 500 delivered possession to the plaintiff, that prior to the registration of the Kabala Khetro Mohan died leaving two sons, Madhu Sudhan Baroi and Bipod Ranjon Baroi as his heirs and the said two sons upon attaining majority sold on 13-5-1969 the land as to which their father entered into contract to sell to the plaintiff; that SA record was wrongly prepared in the name of Ahladi Bewa and Sadhu Charan and about the said wrong record Khetro Mohan Baroi had knowledge; that plaintiff for correction of the record filed Title Suit No. 101 of 1986 in the Sixth Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka for correction of SA and RS Khatian and the same was decreed ex-parte on 27-3-1989 that while plaintiff took steps for correction of the record on the basis of the said decree, it was found that the land in the suit has mutated in the name of the defendant on the basis of the forged kabala; that the plaintiff obtained certified copy of the kabala on 22-9-1990 and on the basis of which defendant claimed the land and filed Mutation Case No. 275 of 1990 before the Assistant Commissioner (land) for correction of the record and in due course plaintiffs got their names mutated by cancelling mutation of defendant Nos. 1 and 2; that the defendant having had suffered defeat in the miscellaneous case threatened the plaintiff on 28-12-1990 to dispossess from the suit land. Hence the suit. 

 16. The suit was contested by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by filing joint written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending, interalia, that the suit is barred by limitation; not maintainable and also that Ahladi Bewa was the original owner and CS Khatian was prepared in her name and that SA record was also recorded in the name of Ahladi Bewa and Sadhu Charan Mondal; that defendants entered into contract with Ahladi Bewa and Keshob Lal on 1-10-1975 and the said persons executed several deeds of agreement for sale and delivered possession to the defendants upon receiving Taka 18,000 and subsequently on 20-4-1985 they executed Sale Deed and the defendants have been living in the land by making construction. 

 24. Mr Tushar Kanti Roy, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court is not a proper judgment of reversal. He further submits that the teamed Appellate Court failed to consider that PW 1 in his deposition stated that Title Suit No. 101 of 1986 was filed for correction of the SA record and got ex-parte decree dated 23-7-1989. But the learned Appellate Court failed to consider that the ex-parte decree was not obtained by fraud or collusively and left it out from consideration. Although the defendants had opportunity to challenge the said judgment by filing an independent suit or challenge the said ex-parte decree in the present suit. He next submits that the learned Appellate Court failed to consider the report submitted by the Chairman Shyampur Union Parishad to the Assistant Commissioner land Tejgaon Circle, Dhaka dated 10-2-1991(Exhibit-7) and certificate of the Chairman Shyampur Union Parishad dated 22-12-1985 (Exhibit-8) and specially Exhibit-5 from which it evident that Ahladi Bewa died long before the independence of Bangladesh and Ahladi Bewa died leaving behind only son Shamboo Nath and Shamboo Nath, who died leaving widow Sreemoti Bewa and PW4 categorically stated that Ahladi Bewa died in the year 1949. He also submits that the plaintiff successfully proved the possession in the suit land by paying rents by Exhibit-11 series. But the lower court failed to find that the plaintiff Md Imam Uddin paid rent in the name of recorded tenant, Ahladi Bewa from 1354 BS to 1363 BS same was paid to the zaminder sheresta whereas zamindar was not entitled to receive rent after 1356 BS. He finally submits that the learned Appellate Court failed to consider that the defendant did not specifically deny about the death of Ahladi Bewa in their written statement hence the same will be taken to be admitted under Order VIII, rule 3 and 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his submissions learned advocate cited decisions reported in 20 DLR 3, 45 DLR 349 and 11 BLT (AD) 139. 

 25. On the other hand, Mr AKM Badrudduza, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 -opposite parties herein submits that the Appellate Court on proper consideration and elaborate discussion and perusal of the evidence and materials on record rightly set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court. He further submits that the trial court clearly found that the plaintiffs did not file the original deed dated 28-4-1952 and 10-5-1969 and they did not state any reasons for not filing the original deed dated 10-5-1969. Though in the plaint they have stated that Madhushudon and Bipod Ranjan executed saf-kabala in favour of the plaintiffs on.13-5-1969 and registered the same in favour of the plaintiffs on 10-5-1969. The Appellate Court observed that deed has been registered before the date of execution. He next submits that the Appellate Court categorically pointed out that the plaintiffs in the suit prayed for cancellation of deed No. 9400 of the defendant dated 21-4-1985 but the plaintiff failed to prove the same by adducing any witness regarding deed that the same was not executed on that date. He also submits that the Appellant Court on careful examination of (Exhibit-5 series) found that the plaintiffs obtained the decree against defendants of present title suit as they were not made party in Title Suit No. 101 of 1986 and the said suit was decreed on ex-parte and further the schedule of the aforesaid two suits are not same. He further submits that the Appellate Court in the judgment clearly found that the plaintiffs claimed the suit land through oral bainanama but in the certified copy of the deed dated 10-5-1969 there was no mention of oral bainanama or contract and none of the PWs made any statement about the oral contract or bainanama in their deposition. He finally submits that the Appellate Court rightly found and came to the conclusion that the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession by oral and documentary evidence as such the learned Advocate prayed for discharge of the rule. Learned Advocate again submits that the trial court erroneously passed the decree although the plaintiffs miserably failed to prove their case that Ahladi Bewa died before liberation war and she was not alive at the time of execution and registration of the sub-kabala dated 21-4-1985. 

 26. Heard the learned Advocate of both the parties, perused the judgment of both the courts below and examined the evidence and materials on record. 

 28. Both the parties adduced oral and documentary evidence to prove their respective cases. In this suit plaintiffs to prove their case produced PW 1 Md Iman Uddin, in examination-in-chief he stated that Ahladi Bewa died leaving only son Shambhuo Nath who died leaving wife Sreemoti Bewa, Sreemoti Bewa transferred the suit land to Khetra Mohan Baroi by registered sale deed dated 28-4-1952 (Exhibit-3), that Khetra Mohan Baroi entered into an agreement with the plaintiffs to sell the suit land on 14-10-1961, prior to the registration of the kabala Khetra Mohan died leaving his two sons namely, Modhu Sudhan Baroi and Bipod Ranjon Baroi upon majority they sold away by registered sale deed on 13-5-1969 the land as to which their father entered into a contract to sell to the plaintiffs. He further stated that the original kabala could not file since it has been lost. So he filed certified copy of the kabala dated 13-5-1969 and same was marked as (Exhibit-4). PW 1 further stated that after obtaining the certified copy of the judgment of the Title Suit No. 101 of 1986 passed by the sixth Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka same was decreed ex-parte. After obtaining certified copy of the judgment and decree, he went to Tohsil Office and found that the SA record stands in the name of defendant Nos. 1 and 2. Thereafter, he filed Miscellaneous Case No. 275 of 1990 for correction of record of rights stands in the name of defendants. Accordingly record was corrected. He also denied that since Ahladi Bewa had no son plaintiffs could not file any paper. PW 3 Modhu Sudhan Baroi son of Khetra Mohan Baroi stated in chief that they owned and possessed the suit land by purchasing from Sreemoti Bewa wife of Shamboo Nath son of Iswar Mali and Ahladi Bewa wife of Iswar Mali. He further stated that they sold the suit land to the present plaintiffs in 1969 and since purchase the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land. He also asserted that at the time of purchase of the land by his father, Ahladi Bewa was dead. In his cross-examination he stated that it is not a fact that Ahladi Bewa sold the suit land to Sadhu Charan Mondol in 1953. He also denied the suggestion that Ahladi Bewa was alive till 1990 and the record of rights was correctly prepared in her name and during her life time she sold the property in 1985 and delivered possession to defendant Nos. 1 and 2. He also denied the suggestion that Ahladi Bewa was a women of without any issue. The execution of kabala is admitted by him. 

 36. Let us now examine whether the findings and decisions given by the appellate court which reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court and dismissed the suit of the plaintiff are based on proper consideration of evidence and materials on record. The appellate court in reversing judgment find that the properties of the two suits schedule are not same and as such held that it could not be said that a decree of Title Suit No. 101 of 1986 did not mean it has been passed against the defendants of Title Suit No. 3 of 1991. We have perused the schedule of Title Suit No. 101 of 1986 and schedule 'ka' of the present Title Suit No. 3 of 1991. It appears that the schedule of both the suit are exactly same. 

 39. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties by referring (Exhibit-cha) submits that Miscellaneous Case No. 275 of 1990 filed by the plaintiffs and by order dated 29-3-1993 stayed the proceeding of miscellaneous case till disposal of the present Title Suit No. 3 of 1991 pending in the third Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Dhaka. But there is no scope for the plaintiff to file an application in the miscellaneous case to stay their present title suit but it is evident from the order dated 24-2-1991(Exhibit-6 series) that AC (Land) Tejgaon circle allowed the said Miscellaneous case. It further appears that the appellate court as well as the trial court rightly did not consider this aspect of the case. Rather it appears from Exhibits-7 and 8 that in the said miscellaneous case Assistant Commissioner inquired the matter though the Chairman Shampur Union Parisad. Accordingly Chairman Shampur Union Parisad submitted inquiry report (Exhibit-7) to the Assistant Commissioner (Land) Tejgoan Circle and the Chairman Shampur Union Parishad issued certificate dated 22-12-1985(Exhibit-8) stating that Ahladi Bewa had died long before the independence. Exhibit-7 speaks that Ahladi Bewa died leaving only son Shamboo Nath and Shamboo Nath died leaving widow Sreemoti Bewa and on the basis of the survey report conducted by the surveyor in miscellaneous case which was filed by the plaintiff for correction of record of right. Accordingly Assistant Commissioner (Land) Tejgaon corrected the record of right and cancelled the record of right published in the name of the defendants by order dated 24-2-1991 (Exhibit-6 series). 

 40. Thus it appears that the trial court upon consideration of Exhibits-4-6 series rightly passed the decree but appellate court without reversing those findings of the trial court erroneously dismissed the suit. It is the duty of the appellate court to decide the appeal on proper consideration of the evidence as whole. But in the present case appellate court reversed the judgment of the trial court without considering the oral and documentary evidence specially (Exhibits 4-6). Thus the impugned judgment is not passed in accordance with the provision of Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In this respect reference may be made in the case reported in 11 BLT (AD)139 = 8 BLC (AD) 77 it has been held that the lower appellate court being final court of fact will have to discuss and reassess the evidence on record independently while either reversing or affirming the findings of the trial court. Specially, in the case of reversal it is more incumbent upon the appellate court to reassess the evidence on record and to arrive at his own independent finding.

2. The circumstances leading to this rule may briefly be stated as follows: The aforesaid suit was brought by the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 against the defendant No. 1 petitioner before me and opposite party Nos. 2 to 10 alleging, inter alia, that the Suit properties originally belonged to one Sreenath Das and on his death the said properties devolved upon the opposite party Nos. 4 to 10. Thereafter these properties were sold in auction in execution of a Rent suit and opposite party No. 2 purchased the property in auction which was subsequently set aside by a suit filed by opposite parties Nos. 4 to 10 but the records of rights of the properties in suit, prepared in the name of opposite party No.2, Mokbul Hossain remained unchanged. Taking advantage of this wrong entry In the record of rights inspite of the aforesaid suit for setting aside the sale, the defendant No. 1 falsely and collusively got a proceeding for arrear rent started in the name of opposite party No. 2 Mokbul Hossain in the office of R.C.C. Bhola and without making the Opposite parties 4 and 10 parties put their property to sale in certificate case No. 358/1965-66 and purchased It In his own name on 29-4-66. But the petitioner No.1 did not get possession in the property in the question which remained in possession of the opposite party Nos. 4 to 10 all along. The plaintiff claim possession of the suit properties from the heirs of Sreenath Das and Gopal Banda-pandaya and they also claim title by adverse possession as well for more than 20 years. The plaintiff; therefore, prayed for declaration that the auction purchase by the defendant petitioner in the aforesaid certificate proceeding No. 359/65-66 is void ability and is not binding upon the plaintiff and for plaintiffs Possessory right by adverse possession In the suit land and for permanent injunction rest raining the defendants from constructing any hut on the Suit-land. Along with the plaint the plaintiff also filed a petition praying for temporary injunction under order 39 Rule 1. C.P.C restraining the defendant from entering into the suit land and erecting any hut, thereon till the disposal of the suit and obtained an ad-interim order of injunction. It appears that. on 8-4-70 the plaintiff filed another application under order 39 rule 2 for the drawing up contempt proceeding against the defendant No. 1, Sultan Ahmed, and 3 others for violation of ad-interim order of injunction passed by the court on 16-12-69 alleging that the defendant No. 1, in violation of the Court's orderof ad-interim injunction, with the help of others has entered into one of the suit plots, namely, 1240, and has erected a chouchala hut of Golpata. 

 "Ordinarily, the decree in a suit should accord with the rights of the parties as they stand at the date of its institution. But where it is shown that the original relief claimed has, by reason of subsequent change of the circumstances, becomes inappropriate, or that, it is necessary to have the decision of the Court on the altered circumstances in order to shorten litigation or to do complete justice between the parties, it is incumbent upon a court to take notice of events which have happened since the institution of the suit and to mould its decree according to the circumstances as they stand at the time the decree is made. Leave to amend may be granted under O.6 R. 17 for this purpose". 

 7. I respectfully agree with the above observation. In this case the amendment has been sought on the basis of allegation that after the institution of the suit the defendant No. 1 has erected hut on the land and it would be in the ends of justice to decide the matter once for all in the suit. I, therefore, hold that the amendment in this case wall rightly allowed by the learned Munsif. In that view of the matter, the present rule is discharged with costs. The suit seems to have been, filed in 1967 and therefore, should be heard as early as possible. Let the records of the case be sent down expeditiously.

It is stated here that in the printed S.A. khatian the name of Mrs. Gulshan Roshan Ali Hijri Still exists an owner in spite of the fact that the Society got its name mutated in the year 1984 in the record of rights with the office of Circle Officer, Tejgaon and paid rents to Mirpur Tashil Office and accordingly the said Assistant Settlement Officer issued notice upon the recorded owner Mrs. Gulshan Hijri at an old address where nobody lives in as much as she died in 1957 and for reasons best known to the Assistant Settlement officer, he did not serve any notice on the occupants of the plots in question who are living there constructing their respective residential houses and huts. The said Assistant settlement Officer, Dhaka recommended for treating the said property as an abandoned property which the Settlement Officer, Dhaka on 08.01.1997 in Miscellaneous Case No. 2103 of 1995 approved treating the properties as abandoned property on the basis of the report of the Assistant Settlement Officer prior to passing the order, but did not give any opportunity of hearing to the owner occupiers and that it appears that the Settlement Officer also did not consult the concern Revenue Office i.e. officer of the Circle Office, Tejgaon, and being aggrieved the petitioners made representation to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka on 24.01.1998 and/or 31.10.1999 but without any result and the property in reference has not been declared abandoned properties under President Order No. 16 of 1972 and also not published in the list of abandoned properties in the Gazette Notification under Ordinance No .54 of 1985; no notice has been served upon the occupiers till date for delivery of possession of the lands in reference declaring the same as abandoned property. It appears that on the basis of the order dated 08.01.1997 passed on an application filed by one Mrs. Shirin Begum and 50 others, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Land), Tejgaon Circle to consider their application for Settlement of the lands in reference and said Assistant Commissioner (Land) has submitted a collusive report on 09.12.1997 but in the report it has been admitted that the petitioners are in possession of the lands, and it now appears that aforesaid Shirin Begum and other are instrumental in the initiation of Miscellaneous Case No. 2103 of 1995 and that having failed to get redress as aforesaid; the petitioners caused service of legal notice on the respondents on 15.11.1999 through their lawyers. The management of the Society as vendors of the petitioners has also obtained a Rule in writ petition No. 3400 of 1998 on 03.11.1998 challenging the impugned decision and on which an order of stay has been granted. 

 5. In view of the above, we do not find any error apparently on the face of the record for our interference with the impugned judgment by way of review. The submissions of the learned Additional Attorney General are relating to merit of the case which has been disposed of on merit.

Petitioner Nos. 2 and 3 predecessor-in-interest of petitioner Nos. 1(a) and 1(b) instituted Title Suit No. 225 of 1986 against the defendant-opposite parties for a declaration of title to the suit land described in schedule to the plaint alleging, inter alia, that the plaintiffs got the suit land by way of inheritance and had been possessing the same but the suit land was wrongly recorded during settlement operation in the name of defendant No. 2 and such wrong record of rights has clouded plaintiffs' title and in order to remove the cloud they were constrained to bring the suit. 

 6. None appeared for the petitioner when the matter was called on for hearing. Heard the learned Deputy Attorney-General for the opposite party and perused the record. 

 7. Mr Helal Uddin Mollah, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for opposite party No.1, submits that both the courts below concurrently found that the plaintiffs have no prima facie title in the suit land and the Government is in possession of the same vide LA Case No. 37 of 1902-3 and the suit land is in possession of the District Judge, Sylhet and the same has correctly been recovered in the name of opposite party No. 2, the Chief Engineer, PWD Dhaka. The learned Subordinate Judge after discussing the materials placed before him and considering the facts and circumstances of the case found that the suit land is in possession of the defendant and the plaintiffs have no prima facie title and possession therein. The learned court of appeal below also after discussing in detail the facts and circumstances of the case came to a finding that the plaintiffs never had any possession in the suit land at least during the last 60 years and that the learned Subordinate Judge was legally justified in passing the impugned order of temporary injunction and restraining the plaintiff petitioners from entering into the suit land pending disposal of the suit. The learned Deputy Attorney-General in support of his contention, referring to the decision in the case of Abdul Matin Chowdhury vs Chapala Rani Sen and others reported in 37 DLR (AD) 205, submits that the concurrent findings of fact by the trial Court and the court of appeal below is binding upon the High Court Division in the 2nd appeal and for that purpose in civil revision unless it could be shown that the suit finding had been vitiated by an error of law or of procedure which had affected the merit of the case. The decision cited by the learned Deputy Attorney-General appears to be applicable in this case. In view of the above facts and circumstances of the case and materials on record and considering the submissions made by the learned Deputy Attorney-General it is found that the learned District Judge was legally justified in passing the impugned order and committed no error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

2. The plaintiff-petitioners claimed settlement of the suit land in raiyati right in favour of one Noor Hossain under defendant No.1, Zilla Parishad Chittagong. The RS record was prepared in his name. While in possession he sold part of the suit land to one Mokbul Ahmed by a registered kabala dated 22- 01-44 and Mokbul Ahmed constructed structures thereon. Mokbul Ahmed sold his purchased portion to Haji Fazlur Rahman and Saleh Ahmed by a registered kabala dated 18-05-48. They were in possession of their respective shares by amicable arrangement. Saleh Ahmed sold his portion to Abdul Mannaf, the predecessor of the plaintiffs, by three kabalas in 1950. Abdul Mannaf constructed pucca and kutcha structures and inducted monthly tenants.  5. Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, learned Counsel for the plaintiff-petitioners submits that the record of rights have all along been prepared in the name of the plaintiffs' predecessors. True, but the plaintiffs could not file any paper to show the alleged raiyati right of Noor Hossain on the basis of settlement or lease taken from defendant No. 1. 3. Mr. M.L. Bhowmik, the learned Advocate has appeared along with Mr. B.K. Das, the learned. Advocate for the petitioner but none has appeared for the opposite party, the Assistant Custodian Contention of Mr. Bhowmik has been based on the decision of Division Bench of this Court reported in 21 D.L.R. 331 as already referred to above. In that case the Deputy Commissioner of a District made an application to be a party in a Probate proceeding under section 283 of the Succession Act alleging that the relevant record of rights contained a wrong entry in favour of the deceased testator who, in fact, got no interest in the property to be bequeathed by the Will but his application was rejected by the High Court on the ground that the Deputy Commissioner was not a necessary party since he got no interest in the land through the deceased testator. I have perused that decision but I find that this decision is not applicable to the instant case since the Custodian of Enemy Property, though he does not claim, interest through the deceased testator, has certainly got every interest in the "Enemy Property" which vested in him under law namely, the Defense of Pakistan Rules and thereafter vested in the Government. 

 4. Mr. B. K. Das concedes that if the property in question is an enemy property then the Custodian has got every interest therein but he has referred to the record of the instant case and has pointed out that there is no prima facie evidence that the property in question is at all an enemy property. The application of the Assistant Custodian itself shows that an Enemy Property case was started in 1978 on the basis of a report of the Tahsildar who however did not state that the deceased testator was ever an enemy alien residing in India in the relevant period; that is during the Indo-Pak. War of 1965. The report of the Tahsildar simply stated that the sons of Satish Chandra. Roy who was the recorded tenant "became his legal heirs but they are Indian nationals". Report does not even state that Satish died in India as an enemy alien or the date of his death nor does it show that the property was enlisted and treated as Enemy Property at any time before it was submitted in 1978, On the other hand, the petitioner filed a certified copy of Death Register of Begumganj Municipality to show that the petitioner's father Satish Chandra Roy died at his house in Noakhali as a Bangladeshi citizen in the year 1975. The Tahsildar's report simply shows that "sons of Satish Chandra are Indian Nationals". Even if his sons are Indian Nationals this fact does not make him an enemy alien or his property an enemy property under the Defense of Pakistan Rules. Mere claim of the Assistant Custodian that the property of the deceased testator is an enemy property in respect of which an enemy property case was started in 1978 is not sufficient for coming to a conclusion that the property is an enemy property. In these circumstances the impugned order allowing addition of party cannot be maintained but the matter may be further enquired into.

2. It is the admitted case that the petitioners caught fish from a tank and took away the same in spite of protest from the complainant. The prosecute ion case is that the complainant took the lease of the tank in question in the Municipality for five years and preserved the fishes there. The defence contended that they purchased the tank in question from the recorded owner. The purchase was made in the name of Rahman Chand Bibi, wife of the petitioner Chand Mia and as such they exercised their bonfire right of claim over the tank in question. The Courts below on assessment of evidence found that the petitioners caught and took away fish without the consent of the complainant. 

 3. Mr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing in support of the Rule bas contended that the learned Magistrate has found at page 10 of his judgment, that there is a bonfire dispute regarding the title of the tank, The lower appellate Court has assumed that the Municipality had been in possession of the tank according to the lower appellate Court otherwise for taking lease the complainant would not spend money for paying the 'salami'. In my opinion this approach to the case in wrong. It is for the prosecution to prove that they bad given possession to the lessee which they had on the basis of which they had in some right the tank. There is nothing in the evidence of the witnesses for the prosecution to show that the Municipality was the owner of the tank P. W. 5 who is an Overseer of the Municipality has said nothing about the ownership of the Municipality over the tank. He has in cross-examination after recall admitted that the record-of-rights stands in the name of Rahman Chand Bibi, the wife of accused Chand Mia. The blower appellate Court has held that from the plot number given in the S. A. Khattan the identity of the tank cannot be established with the identity of the tank purchased by the wife of the petitioner Chand Mia. The C. S  Khatian exhibited on behalf of the petitioner’s shows the Khatian number of the plot in question is 368 and the Plot No. is 2137. The deed exhibit A also shows the same. The admission of P. W. 5 and the deed led the taught Magistrate to hold that there was a bonfire dispute regarding the title of tale tank in question. That being the position it is difficult to accept the finding of the lower appellate Court. As I have already stated the lower Appellate Court moved from the premises that because the complainant has spent money. Therefore, the possession must have been given to him the Municipality after the lease. There is no evidence to show that the Municipality was in possession of the tank in question except the evidence of P. W. 3 and P. W. 5 who in cross examination admitted that the record of right of the tank is in the name of the petitioner Chand Mia. The evidence, therefore, that the complainant is in possession is based on no document of possession or title of the Municipality from whom he got his possession. The lessee must prove that the lessor had the right to grant lease and to deliver possession. That has not been done in this particular case, P. W. 5 has also admitted that there is nothing in writing to show that he was asked by the Municipality to deliver possession to the complainant.

caseno:
Civil Revision No. 474/1986
Civil Revision No. 2601/91
lawyer:
Mansur Habib with Zainul Abedin, Advocates — For the Petitioner 
Adram Hossain Amin, Advocate — For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Serajul Karim Choudhury ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Heirs of deceased Abul Khayer Choudhury
Md Abu Ali Choudury and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
2. The predecessor of the opposite parties Md Abdul Khayer Chowdhury, as plaintiff, has filed another class suit being No.358/78 in the 2nd Court of the Munsif, Rangpur, for declaration of his title to the suit land stating, inter alia, that the disputed land belonged to Wakf Estate of Bhangni Mosque and one Munirunessa Chowdhury made wakf of the suit property along with other property in favour of the said Bhangni Mosque in the year 1287 BS. Munirunnessa remained as Mutoalli of the wakf property during her life and after her death one Enayet Karim Chowdhyry became Mutoalli of the said property of the Mosque. Enayet Karim as Mutoalli of the Mosque appointed Abul Khayer Chowdhury as Moazzin of the Mosque and gave him the suit land in the year 1287 BS to enjoy the same in lieu of his service as Moazzin, Abul Khayer Chowdhury rendered his service as Moazzin and grew crops, created house on plot No.676 and the suit land was recorded in CS Khatian in his name as Chakran for the purpose of giving Azan in the Mosque. When the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into force, the suit land was recorded in the name of Abul Khayer Chowdhury as tenant. Since then Abul ''Khayer Chowdhury has been possessing the suit land till his death. But during life time of Abul Khayer Chowdhury defendant No.1 the present petitioner, the Mutoalli of the Wakf Estate, directed Abul Khayer Chowdhury to surrender the possession of the suit land on 24-9-78. Then he filed the suit for declaration of his title to the suit land, During pendency of the suit Abul Khayer Chowdhury died and his heirs have duly been substituted as plaintiffs. Defendant No.1 the Mutoalli of the Wakf Estate, contested the suit by filing a written statement wherein he stated that previous Mutoalli Enayet Karim Chowdhury, never granted lease of the suit land to Abul Khayer Chowdhury permanently and he appointed Abul Khayer Chowdhury as Moazzin of the Mosque on condition that so long he would discharge his duties properly, he would be entitled to enjoy the suit land as Moazzin and that he would have no right to hold the land after giving up his service or on ceasing to perform his duties, Abul Khayer Chowdhury managed to prepare the record of rights of the suit land in his name and against which the defendant filed an appeal and the said appeal was allowed and the record of right of the suit land was corrected accordingly. Abul Khayer created some collusive sale deeds in respect of the suit land in favour of one Bachcha Mia and his son Abul Ali Chowdhury. Since Abul Khayer Chowdhury did not surrender the possession of the suit land the present Mutoalli applied for his eviction and the same is pending before the Administrator of Wakfs. Abul Khayer Chowdhury ceased to perform his duty since more than 20 years and he had no tenancy right to the suit land, so the suit is liable to be dismissed. The learned Munsif considering the evidences on record decreed the suit. The petitioner then preferred the appeal before the learned District Judge and the said appeal was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge who by his judgment and decree dated 28-5-86 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the trial court''s Judgment. Being aggrieved at and dissatisfied with the above decision the petitioner preferred this application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure to set aside the impugned judgment and decree. 

 3. Mr Mansur Habib, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submitted that the suit land was made wakf in favour of the mosque and, as such, "Allah" becomes the owner of the suit property and the Mutoalli of the Wakf Estate is only a caretaker of the land and he has got no right to settle the land permanently to any person on behalf of Allah and that Allah is not a juristic person according to section 3(39) of the General Clauses Act or rent receiver according to section 2(23) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act-1950 and, as such, section 11 of the said Tenancy Act will not apply in this case. It is admitted that the suit land is a portion of land of Wakf property of Bhangni Mosque and Enayet Karim was the Mutoalli of the said Mosque. It is also admitted that the suit land was given to Abul Khayer Chowdhury for service as Moazzin of Bhangni Mosque and the same was recorded in the CS Khatian as Chakran for giving azan of the Mosque. So the suit land was given to Abul Khayer in lieu of his service of Bhangni Mosque. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submitted that for giving service as Moazzin no one can claim salary according to Muslim law. He referred to Hedaya page 499 translated in English wherein it is stated that First the Prophet has said, read the Quran but do not receive any recompense for so doing, and also directed Oathman Bin Abaseeyes that if he were appointed a Moazzin (a cryer to prayer) he should not take any wages. Accordingly, to that view a Moazzin is not entitled to salary in any way. But the Motualli of the Mosque had given the suit land to Abul Khair for performing his duties that is, for giving Azan, of Bhangi Mosque on condition that when he ceased to give Azan of the Said Mosque he will not be entitled to use the land for cultivation or any other purpose. The said case was given to him for a particular purpose of the Mosque and it has not been settled to him permanently by the then Mutoalli to perform Azan of the Mosque by him and after his death by his heirs or by his nominee. The owner of the property is Bhangni Mosque which is permanent. The land of the Wakf Estate is guided by the Wakf Ordinance. There is no evidence on record that Mutoalli had taken permission from Administrator of the Wakfs to give the suit land to Abul Khayer for his service to the Mosque. There is nothing on record that there is any condition in the wakf deed that the Mutoalli can give land of the Mosque to any person for his service to the Mosque, Against the above submission the learned Advocate for the opposite party Mr. Akram Hossain Amin submitted that Abul Khayer Chowdhury has acquired occupancy right in the suit land after promulgation of EBSA and T Act and according to section 11 of the said Act he is not a tenant under the Government in the land and his name has duly been recorded and that since the suit land was recorded as Chakran Land in the CS Khatian and he continued his tenancy right of said land after promulgation of the EBSA & T Act, 1951 and has been continuously possessing the same, he acquired valid title to the land. The Courts below decreed the plaintiffs title to the suit land taking the view that the same was chakran land of Abul Khayer and, as such, he became tenant according to section 11 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In the Wakf property the owner of which is a Mosque and the Mosque will continue according to Muslim law up to "Day of Judgment "and service of it will continue up to that day. The Chakran land as defined in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is for the person is rent receiver or subordinate rent receiver. After acquisition of interest of such rent receiver the land given to the servant by the rent receiver is liable to be kept by those servants and the same is inheritable as the service of servant is not required by the rent receiver after acquisition of their Estates. But service of the Mosque will continue till Dooms day as it is stated above. In the evidence on record it is found that the Bhangni Mosque is still in existence and the service of the said Mosque Moazzin of giving "Azan" of the said Mosque is continuing and same will continue. In that view of the matter the Chakran land given for Azan of the Mosque cannot be considered as equal to the Chakran land as stated in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. So, the view taken by the court below can not be considered as correct view in respect of the land of Wakf State. Considering this view I find no substance in the submission made by the learned advocate for the opposite party. Since the Wakf land which is given to Allah for the purpose of His House, the Mosque, the said land cannot be alienated by anybody or even by Mutoalli unless condition is laid down in the Wakf deed by the maker. It has already been said that no such condition is found in the record and, as such, it cannot be said that Abul Khair or his heirs can acquire any right to the property without performing the specific duty "Azan" to the Mosque, So in view of the above discussion I find substance in the application. The court: below erred in law in deciding the suit. 

 In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The judgment and decree of both the courts below are hereby set aside and the suit is dismissed without any order as to cost. Send the lower courts record immediately.

3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short is that the suit land originally belonged to Abdul Gafur under land lord Upendra Chandra Basu and the C. S. record was prepared in his name correctly. That before few years of C. S. operation Abdul Gafur kept the suit property mortgaged with Bakshu Sheikh alias Bepari by registered mortgage deed accepting Tk. 250/- from him and handed over possession of the suit land to Bakshu Sheikh @ Bepari; that it was settled that the suit land would be returned by execution of a registered deed if the money is returned. In the C. S. khatian it was recorded that Bakshu Sheikh alias Bepari is in possession of the suit property through cot kabala. That subsequently Mir Abdul Gafur converted that Kot kabala into Sub-kabala by accepting another Tk. 150/-and gave up the claim of the suit land. Bakshu Shiekh possessed the suit land for more than twelve years and after his death his heirs have become the owners of the suit land. That the present plaintiffs are successive heirs of Bakhsu Sheikh @ Bepari. That in the month of Chaitra, 1400 B.S. when the plaintiffs went to pay rent of the suit land in the local Tahsil Office they came to know that the S. A. record of the suit land had been prepared in the name of the defendants and hence the suit. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1-2/7-10 contested the suit by filing written statements denying the claim of the plaintiffs. The material case of the defendants is that Abdul Gafur and Bakshu Sheikh @ Bepari were the original owners of the suit land. Abdul Gafur sold the suit property to Hasen and Hossain-predecessors of these defendants on 25 Chaita, 1340 B.S.at Tk. 95 by oral arrangement and they enjoyed possession of the suit land for more than twelve years and accordingly S. A. record has been prepared in their names; that the claim of the kot kabala and subsequent sale of the suit land to Bakshu Sheikh alias Bepari by Abdul Gafur is not true. 

 5. Both the parties adduced some witnesses before the trial Court in order to prove their respective cases. The trial Court, on consideration of those evidence, dismissed the suit making observations to the effect that the S. A. khatian of the suit land was prepared in the name of the defendants 40 years before, but during this long period the plaintiffs did not take any step to correct the S. A. khatian of the suit land and to pay rent of the suit land and that these facts falsify plaintiffs' case that their predecessor got the suit land from Abdul Gafur and prove the defendants case that Abdul Gafur sold the suit land orally to the predecessors of the defendants. The appellate Court below reversed these findings and decisions of the trial Court on making observations to the effect that according the entry of the C. S. record the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs namely Bakshu Sheikh alias Bepari used to possess the suit land on the strength of 'cot kabala' and that this entry of the C. S. record of rights can not be presumed to be false in the absence of any evidence at all, that in this suit the onus was on the defendants to prove that Abdul Gafur released the suit property from Bakshu Sheikh alias Bepari upon payment of debt, but no such evidence could be adduced by the defendants. The appellate Court below has made observations to the effect also that the defendants have failed to adduce any evidence whatsoever to prove their case that Abdul Gafur sold the suit land orally to their predecessors in the year 1340 B.S. 

 8. Mr. Syed Mahbubur Rahman, the learned Advocate on-record appearing for the respondents has made submissions supporting the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. 

 9. We have gone through the impugned judgment of the High Court Division and those of the appellate Court below and the trial Court. We find that both the appellate Court below and the High Court Division, on correct analysis and appreciation of the evidence on record, rightly found the plaintiffs' right title and possession in the suit land. We find no reason to interfere with the concurrent findings and decisions of the High Court Division and the appellate Court below.

full_judgment:
2. The suit for declaration of title and plaintiff's case, in short, is that suit land was purchased by Kafiron Bibi on 25.10.1922 by registered sale deed No.5159, by sale deed No.903 dated 28.02.1924 and registered sale deed No.5284 dated 08.11.1922 from C.S. recorded tenants and took possession of the same. Kafiron Bibi enjoying the land in question by exercising all acts of possession thereon. Kafiron Bibi died, leaving son Noor Mohammad Mondal as her heir who also enjoyed the land in question by exercising all acts of possession and during his peaceful possession on 20th Ashsin, 1349 B.S. transferred the said land in favour of his wife, Mofizan Bewa, plaintiff, in exchange of her dower money and since then Mofizan Bewa possessing the suit land in question through her husband but beyond her knowledge, S.A. and R.S. record of right of the land were prepared in the name of her husband, Noor Mohammad Mondal. Noor Mohammad Mondal died in 1971 leaving, Mofiza Bewa and his 2nd wife and other defendants as his heirs. At the end of Magh, 1405 B.S. defendants approached the plaintiff and demanded partition of the land in question as heirs of Noor Mohammad Mondal by dint of R.S. khatians prepared in the name of Noor Mohammad Mondal. Plaintiff after obtaining certified copy of R.S. khatian on 11.01.1999 came to know the erroneous preparation and publication of S.A. and R.S. khatians, hence the suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos.1, 2, 5 and 10-14 contested the suit by filing joint written statement, denying the plaint case. It is their case that suit land owned and possessed by one, Kafiron Bewa who died leaving son Noor Mohammad and 3 daughters, Feli alias Muni Bibi, Afizan Bibi and Mirjan Bibi as heirs. S.A. record of right was duly prepared and published in their names along with the heirs of other C.S. recorded tenants. S.A. recorded tenant Gamir Uddin Mondal and others filed Other Class suit No.68 of 1965 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Rajshahi against Noor Mohammad Mondal and his sisters, Muni Bewa and Mirjan and heirs of Afizan. Ultimately the said suit was decreed on the basis of solenama between the plaintiffs and defendant Nos.1-4, 6-12, 14-16 and 19. During R.S. operation suit land has duly been recorded in the name of Noor Mohammad. Noor Mohammad subsequently died, leaving his first wife, Mafizan, plaintiff, 2nd wife Alekjan Bibi and 3rd wife, Most. Fatema Bewa, defendant No.5 and sons of Noor Mohammad Mondal, defendant Nos.1, 2, 3 and 4 and 9 daughters, defendant Nos.6-9 and 10-14 as heirs and they all entered into ejmali possession of the suit land. Noor Mohammad Mondal never transferred the suit land to plaintiff by patta in exchange of her dower money and she never enjoyed and possessed the suit land by herself alone. Noor Mohammad Mondal and the plaintiff, has manipulated and fabricated the alleged patta in the name of plaintiff only to deprive his step brothers, sisters and step mothers, filed the instant false stilt, is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. Mr. Noor Nabi, learned Advocate, appeared for the defendant-petitioners, submits that court of appeal below without considering material on record and without considering that plaintiff's are not in possession of the suit land and suit land did not possess by her husband but through her husband who possessing the suit land after his death, the suit land was in ejmali possession of the heirs of Noor Mohammad Mondal as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to set aside. Learned Advocate further submits that in allowing appeal and decreeing the suit court of appeal below did not reverse the findings of trial court as regard fairness of patta which the learned Judge of trial court empathetically found. 

 6. Only question calls for determination as to whether patta in favour of plaintiff by her husband is genuine or not. Trial court held that patta is a spurious document as writing of patta has been smeared by soaking and plaintiff failed to prove possession pursuant to the patta. Appellate court in the body of the judgment found that plaintiff possessing the suit land and D.W.1 in his cross-examination admitted that suit property is her own property. P.Ws in their depositions proved patta exhibit-4, P.W.2 proved hand writings of Noor Mohammad Mondal. It is in the evidence that exhibit-4 was exhibited without any objection. Defendant's case is that suit land was not in possession of plaintiff by herself. In our country, it is the go of the day women are shaky in proving that she is in possession of the suit land. Moreover, it is in record that plaintiff is a pordanshin lady. S.A. and R.S. record was prepared in the name of her husband, Noor Mohammad Mondal. Learned Judge of the appellate court considers "Record of right does not create or extinguish the title, it merely raises a presumption of accuracy but the presumption is rebuttable (AIR 1963 Ori. 29; AIR 1968 Pat. 450 at 453). It is no evidence of title, 2 Cal. LJ page 305" Against wrong preparation of record of right, limitation is 6 (six) years for filing suit for declaration, is not applicable when it is proved plaintiffs are in possession for long period. 

 A suit for declaration of title on the ground of wrong record of rights instituted beyond 6(six) years of publication thereof is not barred by limitation when the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land for long period. Learned Judge also relied on 10 MLR (AD) 66. 

 9. Send down the lower court records.

2. The facts, in short, are that the respondents purchased the case land in December, 1974 by three kabalas and had their names duly recorded in the records of right. The respondents claim that since then they have been paying the rent regularly. On the application by the respondents on 27-6-1996 the petitioners approved the plan of the respondents for the construction of two nine-storied buildings and one sixteen-storied apartment building on the case land. Accordingly, the respondents started the construction at a cost of huge sum of money obtained from the bank. The respondents publicised forward sale of the apartments and granted several advance bookings for such sales against payments made by the intending buyers. While the construction was going on in full swing the petitioner No.3, the Authorised Officer of RAJUK, issued the impugned memo dated 27-5-1998 cancelling the plan on the allegation that correct information regarding the project was not supplied by the respondents with their application for approval of the plan. The order was passed without serving any notice of show cause on the respondents and without giving them an opportunity of being heard. The respondents preferred an appeal on 9-6-1998 before the appeal committee of petitioner No. 1 (RAJUK) under section 115 of the Building Construction Act. Since the hearing and disposal of the appeal was being delayed the respondents moved the High Court Division and obtained a Rule after serving a notice of demand of justice. 

 3. The petitioners contested by  submitting that the writ petition was not maintainable in view of the pendency of the appeal against the impugned  order and the Rule issued by the High Court Division had become infructuous in view of the order of the said appeal committee on 7-9-1998. The petitioner's further case is that, as per decision of the Government for extension of Gulshan Model Town the entire land of Plot No. 360 measuring 3.01 acres was requisitioned in Land Acquisition Case No. 10 of 1963-64 and about 90% of the compensation money had been paid to the land owners and the possession of the requisitioned lands were officially handed over to the Dhaka Improvement Trust. However, a decision was taken in 1970 to derequisition the lands and accordingly, a few notices were served on some of the land owners asking them to refund the compensation paid to them. Subsequently, the decision was reviewed and cancelled before any gazette notification of the decision was made. The respondents could not show any paper to the High Court Division in the writ petition that the case land was derequisitioned or the possession thereof was restored to their predecessors-in-interest of the respondents upon refund of compensation money. Therefore, any mistaken approval of plan and mutation of names in the record of rights do not have any bearing on the question of title and possession of the case land in question.

2. The petitioner instituted Other Suit No. 650 of 1978 on 13.6.1978 in the court of Munsif Sadar Mymensingh, against the opposite party No. 1 and another for declaration of title in respect of 0.15 acres of land appertaining to plot No. 2263 of CS Khatian No. 171/199 and ROR Khatian No. 1 of mouza Fulbaria on the allegations inter alia, that the petitioner was the owner of the said land but in the last ROR operation the said land was, wrongly recorded in khatian No. 1 in the name of the government as khas land. The opposite party No. 1 claimed title in thy said land on the basis of settlement which created cloud over the title of the petitioner. The opposite party No. 1 and the petitioner on 10.9.1982 filed a petition of compromise in the said suit and the opposite party No. 1 admitted the title of the petitioner. Sub-sequent, the opposite party No. 1 on 16.2.1983 filed an application for not recording compromise on the basis of the said compromise petition. The petitioner objected to the said application. The learned Munsif, however on 10.4.1983 rejected the compromise petition leading to filing Miscellaneous Appeal No. 82 of 1983 in the court of District Judge, Mymensingh. The said appeal and the suit are pending before the courts for disposal. 

 5. Next, she submits that the learned Munsif committed an error in law in holding that the claims in the two suits are different and upon such erroneous view wrongly rejected the application. She submits that in an application under section 10 CPC the relief sought for is immaterial either for allowing or rejecting the application. She submits that the subject matter in issue is material and not the claim of the parties. She further submits that the learned Munsif also committed an error to say that the relief’s claimed in the two suits are not same. She contends that in the earlier suit filed by the petitioner the relief sought for was that the petitioner is the owner of the land in suit and preparation of the record of rights in the name of the Government under khas khatian was wrong. In the subsequent suit also the relief sought for was that the Government is the owner of the land. Therefore, she submits that in both the suits the subject matter relates to ownership of the land in suit which requires adjudication by the courts. From the record it seems to me that the contention of the learned Advocate has substance. In aid of her submission she cites the decision in the case of Sakhawat Hossain Vs. Chowdhury Muhammad Sarwar and others, PLD 1968 Dac 557 wherein it has been held that the difference in the relief claimed in the two suits is quite immaterial under section 10 of the Code. A careful examination of the provision of section 10 CPC seems to me that the matter in issue in the previously instituted suit and in the subsequent suit is material consideration for the court in an application under section 10 CPC and not the relief sought for in the said suits. The case of Sakhawat Hossain also supports this view of mine. Accordingly; I set aside the impugned order and allow the application filed by the petitioner under section 10 CPC and direct to stay the trial of the Title Suit No. 92 of 1983 pending in the court of Upazila Munsif, Fulbaria, District Mymensingh.

Vs
Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, 
Ministry of Land Bangladesh, Dhaka and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Naima Haider J: In this application under Article 102 of the Constitution, Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the inclusion of the petitioner No. 1 company's 123 decimals of land situated at Mouza-Zamur and Mouza-Zamur Muchipara having RS Khatian Nos. 295, 110, 114, 107 and RS Dag Nos. 304, 49, 50 & 51 under Police Station-Savar, District-Dhaka as per the decision of the respondent No. 2 (i.e. the Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka Division) dated 1-12-2011 in LA Case No. 2/2011-2012 shall not be declared to have been made and issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and why inclusion of the petitioner No. 1 company's said land shall not be declared arbitrary, malafide and discriminatory and to be violative of the fundamental rights guaranteed to the petitioners under Articles 27, 31, 40 and 42 of the Constitution and further as to why the respondents shall not be directed to exclude the said land of the petitioner company from the proceeding of LA case No. 2/2011-2012. 

 3. Facts necessary for the disposal of the Rule is that: The petitioner No. 1 is a private limited Company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1913. It carries on business, inter-alia, of manufacturing and exporting of readymade garments and sweaters and wearing apparels of all kinds. It is a sister concern of Unifill Group, one of the renowned Business Groups in Bangladesh. The petitioner No. 2 Mr M Sakhawat Hossain, Barrister-at-Law is an Advocate of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Bangladesh, who holds substantial number of shares in the petitioner No. 1 company and, as such, he has sufficient interest in the subject matter of this Writ Petition and hence, he has been included as the petitioner No. 2 to enforce the fundamental rights as guaranteed under Articles 27, 31, 40 and 42 of the Constitution. 

 11. When the petitioner company after doing all the needful wanted to start construction of factory building for its compliant garments in the said land, with utter shock and surprise came to know that the respondent No. 3 initiated proceedings to acquire the petitioners land for the purpose of transferring Police Line Mill barrack from Dhaka to Savar. As soon as the petitioner company came to know about the said acquisition proceedings being LA Case No. 2/2011-2012, the concerned officials of the petitioner company rushed to the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka (respondent No. 3) and enquired into the matter. During such enquiry, it was detected that a notice under section 3 of Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 (hereinafter also referred to as the said Ordinance) was issued to various persons including the previous record-holders of the petitioners land, but no notice under section 3 of the said Ordinance was issued to the petitioner company. Thus, the concerned person of the petitioner company immediately filed Preliminary Objection to the office of respondent No. 3. 

 12. Having regard to the objections raised by the petitioner company, the respondent Nos. 4 and 5 vide letter dated 17-8-2011 (process No. 51 dated 18-8-2011) served notice to the Managing Director of the petitioner company and asked him to submit relevant title deeds and records of rights in support of its title and fixed a date on 24-8-2011 at 10-00 am for submitting the same (Annexure G). In order to protect the land from the impugned acquisition proceedings initiated by the respondent No. 3, the petitioner company gave a representation on 13-8-2011 in the form of Written Objection with reasonable details. The petitioner company also made representation to the Secretary, Ministry of Land and the Hon'ble State Minister for Law, Justice & Parliamentary Affairs Government of Bangladesh for excluding the land of the petitioner company from the proposed acquisition of land (Annexure H series). Petitioner company also submitted all its title deeds and record of rights to the office of the respondent No. 3 on 24-8-2011. But the respondents did not take any initiate in this regard. 

 15. Mr M Sakhawat Hossain, (the petitioner No. 2) learned Advocate-in-person submits that as per section 4' of Sub-section (2) of the said Ordinance every objection under section 4 of Sub-section (1) shall be made to the Deputy Commissioner (i.e. respondent No. 3) in writing and the respondent No. 3 shall give the Objector an opportunity of being heard either in person or by an agent and shall, after hearing all such objections and after making such further enquiry, if any, as he thinks necessary, prepare report containing his opinion on the objections. Although serious objection was raised by the petitioner company to the respondent No. 3 regarding the proposed acquisition proceedings vides its letter dated 13-8-2011 but the respondent No. 3 did not give the petitioner company any opportunity of being heard either in person or by an agent in gross violation of section 4 of sub-section (2) of the said Ordinance. When the Managing Director of the petitioner company submitted the relevant title deeds and records of rights to the office of the respondent No. 3 on 24-8-2011 he had also submitted a written objection in the Prescribed Form and these are lying with the office of the respondent Nos. 3 and 4. Petitioner company also vide its letter dated 14-12-2011 requested the respondent No. 3 to give a hearing on the basis of its objection by enclosing therewith the said letter of objection dated 13-8-2011. 

 16. As per the said Ordinance, respondent No. 3 (i.e the Deputy Commissioner), after preparing report in terms of section 4, sub-section (2), if the property exceeds 50 standard bighas of land shall submit the report of the proceedings held by him together with his report for the decision of the Government and if the property does not exceed 50 bighas of land shall submit the record of the proceedings held by him together with his report for the decision of the Divisional Commissioner. Section 5 of the said Ordinance provides that the Government or as the case may be, the Divisional Commissioner after considering the report submitted by the Deputy Commissioner under section 4, sub-section (3) of the said Ordinance shall make a decision about the acquisition of the property and such decision of the Government or as the case may be, the Divisional Commissioner shall be final. 

 30. Relying on Dr Nurul Islam's case, reported in 33 DLR (AD) 201 it was held in the case of Dr Abu Ahmed Chowdhudy vs Bangladesh BLD 98 = 34 DLR 21 that Government did not apply its mind as to why among 34 doctors who completed 25 years of service, the petitioner should be singled out for compulsory retirement. Such retirement must be held discriminatory and violative of fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 27 and 29 and also 135 of the constitution. 

 31. Relying on the decisions of the preceding paragraphs, Mr M Sakhawat Hossain submits that the respondent No. 2 and 3 have totally failed to follow the underlying policy guidelines before exercising their wide discretion and, as such, final decision of the respondent No. 2 should be held discriminatory, arbitrary and violative of fundamental rights guaranteed under Article 27 (Equality before law) of the Constitution. 

 32. Mr M Sakhawat Hossain next points out that the inclusion of land of the petitioner company itself is arbitrary and discriminatory exercise of powers and, as such, the same has affected the fundamental rights of the petitioners as guaranteed under Articles 27, 31 and 40 of the Constitution. The right to property is protected under Article 42 of the Constitution and, as such, the land of the petitioner company cannot be taken away without due process of law and the respondents have also violated the principles of natural justice and legitimate expectation of the petitioners for not excluding their land from the said LA Case. Thus, for violation of Article 27 of the Constitution and legitimate expectation, in the case of Bangladesh Biman Corporation vs Rabia Bashri Irene, 55 DLR (AD) 132, Appellate Division held that 

 "It is now settled law that where an authority makes an order in exercise of a quasi-judicial function, it must record its reasons in support of the order it makes. Every quasi-judicial order must be supported by reasons. The rule requiring reasons to be given in support of an order is, like the principle of audi alteram partem, a basic principle of natural justice which must inform every quasi-judicial process and this rule must be observed in its proper spirit and mere pretence of compliance with it would not satisfy the requirement of law". 

 49. An administrative order must be a reasoned one. Fairness and transparency of administrative decisions require to be recorded. The requirement of recording reasons by every quasi-judicial or even an administrative authority entrusted with the task of passing an order adversely against an individual and communication thereof to the affected persons is one of the recognized facets of the rules of natural justice and violation thereof has the effect of vitiating the order passed by the authority concerned. Hence we further observe that the final acquisition order dated 1-12-2011 passed by the Divisional Commissioner (respondent No. 2) was not reasoned one. We think that giving of reason is an essential element of administration of justice and it is a requirement of law.

Mr. Muhammad Korban Ali with Mr. Md. Fakhar Uddin, Advocate ------ for the petitioner.
