full_judgment:
Mr. A. K. Badrul Huq, J: By this application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure concurrent divisions recorded by the courts below in granting temporary injunction in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party has been challenged by the defendant- petitioners whereupon rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the order of confirmation of temporary injunction passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Sixth Court, Dhaka on 11.8/98 in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 100 of 1998 arising out of a judgment and order of temporary injunction passed by the Assistant Judge, Sixth Court, Dhaka in title suit No. 156 of 1997 dated 22.4.1998 should not be set aside. 

 3. For the purpose of answering to the said questions posed, factual Canvass of the matter IS adverted to which is set out hereunder in a nutshell. The opposite party No. 1 St. Francis Xavier Girls High School being represented by its Head Mistress and Secretary as plaintiff laid a suit being Title Suit No. 156 of 1997 in the Sixth Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka against the defendant petitioners Lakohmi Bazar Shahi Masjid Committee represented by its Chairman and another for a decree of permanent injunction with respect to the suit property detailed in the schedule to the plaint with the averments that the said school was established in the year 1912 and was being run in accordance with the secondary and the Higher Education Board Regulation 1977. One Sree Rajendra Chandra Dey Singh was the owner of the suit property along with other properties and one P.J, Hurth, Bishop of Roman Catholic Church purchased the suit property by way of deed of conveyance registered on 1.4.1902. P.J. Hurth established plaintiff school, St. Gregory Boys High School and a Roman Catholic Church. The plaintiff school has been running since the year 1912. The school is situated on state acquisition plot No. 802 and the area of the suit property is 2.75 acres and during the all previous Record of Rights plaintiff schools name was record-ed. The plaintiff School has been exercising acts of ownership and possession on the suit property on regularly paying rents to the Government and also taxes to the Municipal corporation now city corporation, Dhaka. The defendant Lakshmi Bazar Mosque Is situated on state acquisition plot No. 803. The plaintiff School and defendant Mosque are situated on two different plots. On 10.12.1996 in the morning when the plaintiff school engaged labourers to cut a Tree, the president and secretary of the Masjid Committee and some outsiders obstructed the cutting of the said Tree and claimed the suit property to be the property of Mosque. The plaintiff School asserts that it has exclusive right, interest and the defendant got no right, title, interest and possession there-on. The defendant on 25.5.1997 again attempted to dispossess the plaintiff school from the suit property and G.D. entry being 1475 was registered with Sutrapur police station on 25.5.1997. The plaintiff school, thereafter, has been con-strained to lay the suit for a decree of permanent Injunction before the court. 

 5. The defendant-petitioners resisted the said application for temporary injunction by presenting a written objection traversing all the material allegations made in the plaint as well as the petition for temporary injunction contending inter alia that one pious Muslim built a Mosque during the Mughal period and dedicated the suit property in the name of "Allah". There was an Hujrakhana for the Imam of the Mosque and the Imam used to stay there. On the fall of Nabab Serajddoula the then East India Company for the education of the children of its English employees forcibly possessed the grave-yard and other land of the Mosque. During the cadastral Survey Record of Right .0784 acres of land stood recorded in the Khatian No. 8941 in the name of Moulvi Ibrahim, the Mutwalli. The stand taken by the defendants is that during the state Acquisition record of Right .0180 acres of land stood recorded in the name of the plaintiff school and the record of Right had been prepared by the plaintiff in collusion with the settlement officers. The defendant did never threaten the plaintiff, nor did attempt to enter into the suit property. The defendants assert that the plaintiff got no prima facie and arguable case in the matter of getting an order of injunction. 

 6. The Learned Assistant Judge by the judgment and order dated 22.4.1998 allowed the prayer of the temporary injunction and restrained the defendants from disturbing or interfering with the peaceful possession of the plaintiff school over the suit property. In allowing the prayer for temporary injunction the learned Assistant Judge recorded the following decisions : i) On scrutiny of the C. S. and S. A. Khatian it appears that name of the plain-tiff School had been recorded in the said two records of Right; ii) The plaintiff had submitted the registered deed of conveyance dated 1.4.1902, the Rent Receipts showing payment of rent and the tax receipts showing payment of taxes to Dhaka city corporation. But on the other side the defendants could not produce any paper in support of their claims of title over the suit property. iii) The property of the plaintiff school and the property of the defendant Mosque are on different plots in different Khatians. The defendant could not pro-duce any paper evidencing that .0180 acres of land was recorded as excess in the name of the plaintiff. 

 7. That learned judge, ultimately on careful consideration of materials brought on record recorded the positive finding that the plaintiff school apparently is in possession and got also prima facie and arguable case. 

 10. Granting of injunction in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party having been the controversy in the rule, the principles of issuance and non-issuance of injunction may conveniently be noticed. Injunction is a judicial process by which a party is required to do or refrain from doing any act. Rule 1 of Order 39 of the Code of Civil Procedure primarily concerns with the preservation of the property in dispute till the rights or claims of the parties are adjudicated finally. Injunction is in the nature of preventive relief to a litigant to prevent future possible injury. It is merely provisional in nature and does not conclude a right which is required to be determined on the final adjudication of the suit touching the controversy arising between the parties. Its sole object is to preserve the subject matter of the controversy without determining any question of right. To put it differently the court in exercise of power of granting temporary injunction is to preserve the subject matter of the suit in status-quo for the time being. Of course the grant of temporary injunction is no doubt a discretionary relief and the discretion exercised by the court must not be arbitrary but sound and reasons guided by the judicial principles and capable of correction by the Superior Courts. 

 12. Admittedly, state Acquisition Record of Right stands in the name of the plaintiff school. The claim of the defendant Mosque that the record of right standing in the name of the plaintiff school is wrong cannot be determined in this interlocutory matter like temporary injunction and that can be decided only by legal evidences on the institution of a proper suit to that effect. The plaintiff has filed Rent Receipts showing payment of rent to the Government and also City Corporation or Municipal Tax Receipts evidencing payment of taxes to the city corporation. This payment of rent to the Government and Tax to the city corporation prima facie manifests plaintiffs possession on the suit property and the plaintiff is entitled to get an order of injunction at least to preserve the subject matter in dispute in status quo. The Learned Senior Assistant Judge considered payment of rents to the Government and payment of taxes to city corporation and found a prima facie and arguable case in favour of the plaintiff. The Learned Assistant judge also considered the balance of convenience and inconvenience of the parties and decided the same in favour of the plaintiff. The court of appeal also considered all these aspects and maintained the decisions recorded by the Learned Assistant Judge. The factors which have been relied upon by the courts below for grant of temporary injunction indicate that the exercise of discretion was in accordance with the settled principles of law relating to grant of interlocutory injunction. This court exercising revisional authority under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure will not interfere with the exercise of discretion of the courts below except where the discretion has been shown to have been exercised arbitrarily or capriciously or perversely or where the courts ignored the settled principles of law regulating grant or refusal of interlocutory injunction. Applying the above rule indicating the scope of interference in revision against the exercise of discretion of the courts below to grant the interlocutory injunction. I find no ground to take a different view or to interfere with the grant of interlocutory injunction. 

 13. No points survives on the basis of which the defendant petitioners can seek upsetting the impugned orders and the decisions recorded by the courts below can be quashed in the exercise of revision-al authority under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. No interference is, therefore, called for.

2. Md Ibrahim (the predecessor-in-interest of the present appellant), as plaintiff, instituted the above mentioned Title Suit No. 190 of 1998 impleading the respondent herein as the sole defendant for declaration that the defendant is 'benamder' of the plaintiff in respect of the properties described in schedule `Ka' and 'Kha' to the plaint and also for declaration of his title in those properties. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the land of schedule 'Ka' originally belonged to Samon Rishi and CS Khatian was prepared in his name. Samon Rishi died leaving two sons, named Hari Mohan and Rai Mohan. Hari Mohan died leaving wife Brahmo Rishi and son Bhagoban Rishi. Bhagoban Rishi died unmarried leaving mother Brohma Rishi as sole heir. That Brahmo Rishi while in possession of her share sold out that to Adu Bepari by kabala dated 14-5-1920. That Rai Mohan, the other son of Samon Rishi died leaving five sons, namely, Rajendra, Kutishar, Naba Rishi, Debendra and Surja Mohan and wife Bidhya Rishi. The said heirs of Rai Mohan transferred their share in favour of Adu Bepari by three registered sale deeds dated 16-7-1920, 18-8-1920 and 12-1-1921. That Adu Bepari thus became the owner of those lands. Adu Bepari leased out 0.0636 acre of land to Nobendra Rishi, Broja Kumar Rishi and Shita Nath Rishi and kept the remaining 0.0774 acre of land in his khas possession. Subsequently Adu Bepari sold out those 0.0774 acre of land to Ganga Charan Saha by kabala dated 12-6-1923. Ganga Charan Saha subsequently sold that land to Bhagaban Chandra Bhowmik by kabala dated 26-1-1927. Bhagaban Chandra Bhowmik subsequently transferred the said land to Kanai Lal Gope by kabala dated 22-2-1939. Kanai Lal Gope while in possession, leased out the same land to the plaintiff by registered deed of lease dated 11-4-1952; said Kanai Lal Gope executed a deed of sale also in respect of the said property in favour of the plaintiff on 12-4-1952 which was registered on the same date. That the plaintiff, out of love and affection, purchased the said land in the name of the defendant who is his cousin and sister-in-law; that plaintiff paid the entire consideration money and purchased the same for his own interest and benefit; that the defendant had no means to pay the consideration. That to maintain the benami character of the suit land the plaintiff had the subsequent record of rights recorded in the name of his 'benamdar'. The plaintiff is in possession of the 'Ka' schedule land. He established a mill under the name and style "Ibrahim Machinery Manufacturing Company" in this 'Ka' scheduled land. 

 6. Leave to appeal against this judgment of the High Court Division was granted by this Division to consider the submissions of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-leave-petitioner mainly to the effect that the appellate court below, on consideration of the evidence adduced by both the parties and also the very fact that the defendant did not deny the plaintiffs case that he purchased the 'Kha' scheduled land in the 'benami' of the defendant, rightly decreed the suit, but the High Court Division without referring any evidence on record and pointing out any non-consideration or mis-appreciation of evidence on record by the court of appeal below erroneously and illegally set-aside the well-reasoned judgment and decree of the court of appeal below. 

 7. Mr Anwarul Azim Khair, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-appellant has made submissions before us to the effect that in this suit for declaration of a transaction as 'benami' the plaintiff adduced sufficient evidence-both oral and documentary-to prove all the factors necessary for proving benami purchases; that the evidence adduced by the plaintiff have proved clearly that he paid the consideration money and he has also been possessing the suit land since his purchase; that the plaintiff has also produced the kabala deed showing purchase of the suit land and all other previous transfer deeds relating to the suit land. The learned Advocate has argued that the appellate court below, the last court of facts, on consideration of all these evidence adduced by the plaintiff and also the evidence adduced by the defendant and other facts and circumstances decreed the suit on making elaborate discussion of evidence and also assigning reasons, but the High Court Division without adverting to the reasonings arrived at by the appellate court below and also without considering the evidence adduced by the parties at all most whimsically set-aside the well-reasoned judgment of the appellate court below and restored those of the trial court. The learned Advocate has argued that the judgment of the trial court, in fact, is no judgment at all in the eye of law inasmuch as in this judgment the huge evidence adduced by the plaintiff was not considered at all, that the trial court dismissed the suit on the main reasoning that there was no reason for the plaintiff to purchase the suit land in the 'benami' of the defendant and that the title deed of the suit land came from the custody of the defendant and that the plaintiffs wife deposed in this suit supporting the case of the defendant. The learned Advocate has argued also that the High Court Division committed more wrong and illegality in restoring the judgment and decree of the trial court making observations to the effect that the plaintiff did not examine a single witness to prove his alleged 'benami' purchase of the suit land and to prove the payment of consideration money by him. The learned Advocate has argued that these observations of the High Court Division are absolutely wrong inasmuch as in this suit the plaintiff examined as many as six-witnesses and also adduced bundle of documentary evidence which have been marked as exhibit and all of which have proved sufficiently that the plaintiff purchased the suit land and he paid the consideration money; that the High Court Division also without examining the evidence on record most illegally and erroneously held that the title deed of the suit land came from the custody of the defendant. The learned Advocate has made submissions to the effect also that in this suit the plaintiffs specific case is that Kanai Lal Gope-the original owner of the suit land settled the suit land with him by a registered lease deed dated 11-4-1952 and on the same date he also sold his rent receiving interest in the suit land in favour of the plaintiff by registered kabala and that the plaintiff took that kabala also in the name of the defendant, but the defendant could produce the lease deed only in respect of the suit land which has been marked as Exhibit-'Ka' and the kabala deed-the exahibit-13 and all other previous transfer deeds in respect of the suit land and also the rent receipts, tax receipts, electricity bills, gas bills, water bills etc. in respect of the suit land came before court from the custody of this plaintiff, but neither the trial court nor the High Court Division took into consideration this most important fact that a bundle of title deeds and also various receipts in respect of the suit land came from the custody of the plaintiff, rather the High Court Division, in the impugned judgment most erroneously held that the plaintiff could not adduce any document or any other proof to prove his purchase of the suit land in the 'benami' of the defendant. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff-appellant has made submissions to the effect also that in this suit the admitted facts are that the defendant is the cousin and also the sister-in-law of the plaintiff and that the plaintiff being issueless was very much affectionate to the defendant who lost her husband at her tender age and thereafter used to reside with the plaintiff and his wife in the same house. The learned Advocate has made argument to the effect also that in this suit the plaintiff claimed to have purchased both the 'Ka' scheduled land and 'Kha' scheduled land in the 'benami' of the defendant and the defendant though denied the claim of the plaintiff in respect of the `Ka' scheduled land only, but she did not raise any claim in respect of the `Kha' scheduled land and thereby she rather admitted the plaintiff's case that he purchased the 'Kha' scheduled land in the 'benami' of the defendant. The learned Advocate has argued that this very admitted fact that the plaintiff purchased the `Kha' scheduled land in the 'benami' of the defendant was ignored by both the trial court and the High Court Division though this fact was very much important in this suit to be considered. The learned Advocate has contended that this very admitted fact that the plaintiff purchased the 'Kha' scheduled land in the 'benami' of the defendant coupled with the evidence adduced by the plaintiff prove sufficiently that the plaintiff purchased the 'Ka' scheduled land also in the 'benami' of the defendant. The learned Advocate has argued that the appellate court below, on consideration of all these facts and circumstances and evidence on record rightly decreed the suit of the plaintiff, but the High Court Division without at all adverting to these findings and decision of the appellate court below and also the reasonings thereof most arbitrarily and illegally set-aside the well-reasoned judgment of the appellate court below and restored that of the trial court which was not at all sustainable in law. 

 8. Mr Md Asaduzzaman, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-respondent has made submissions supporting the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. The learned Advocate has made argument to the effect that both the trial court and the High Court Division rightly disbelieved the plaintiffs case of his 'benami' purchase of the 'Ka' scheduled property. The learned Advocate has argued that in fact there was no reason for the plaintiff to purchase the suit land in the 'benami' of the defendant who was his sister-in-law; that the own wife of the plaintiff has deposed in this suit as DW 2 denying the claim of the plaintiff and stating that the defendant purchased the 'Ka' scheduled land with her own money; that both the trial court and the High Court Division, on consideration of evidence of the plaintiff's wife and other facts and circumstances rightly disbelieved the case of the plaintiff and rightly dismissed the suit; that the appellate court below on misinterpretation and mis-appreciation of the evidence on record decreed the suit of the plaintiff illegally. The learned Advocate has made argument to the effect that the impugned judgment of the High Court Division concurring with the findings and decision of the trial court does not suffer from any wrong or infirmity and, as such, this appeal is liable to dismissed. 

 9. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides and gone through the impugned judgment of the High Court Division, those of the appellate court below and the trial court and the evidence on record.

Short facts are that the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 272 of 1987 in the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Barisal for a decree for partition with a prayer for declaration that the kabala dated 23.12.1920 in favour of the defendant is void stating, inter alia, that 60 decimals of land of Mouza Kashipur under R.S. Khatian No. 199 of the same mouza belonged to Sona Gazi and Nasaruddin in 8 annas share each. 48 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian No.146, 3.03 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian No.161, 13 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian No.226, 91 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian No.240, 1.23 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian No.241, 6 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian No.293 belonged to Nasaruddin alone and C.S. record was correctly prepared and finally published. Nasaruddin died leaving behind his only son Hamijuddin who inherited the property. After his death, Sarbanu and her daughter Somartaban inherited 2 annas 13 gondas 1 kara 1 kranti and out of the remaining land, the brother of Sarbanu inherited 2 annas 13 gandas 1 kara 1 kranti. Somartaban died leaving behind two sons and two daughters as her heirs who inherited her share. The share of Hamijuddin was inherited by his sons and daughters, defendant Nos.1-6. Sarbanu had no other name like Sawrupjan and Sarbanu was never married to Ludu Mollah. Hamijuddin in order to deprive his full sister, Somartaban Bibi created a forged, fabricated document on 23.12.1920 and no possession was delivered and no consideration money passed. When Somarthaban Bibi was given in marriage with Safar Molla her husband Safar Molla erected homestead in a portion of the land wherein Hamijuddin lived with his wife Somarthaban Bibi. After the death of Safar Mollah, plaintiff had been residing in the suit land. Record of right was not prepared in the name of Sarbanu but it was prepared in the name of Hamijuddin who had no possession in the entire suit land. Hamijuddin collusively got the record of rights prepared in his name and there is no basis for R.S. and S.A. record. Hence the suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos.2.3 and 6 filed a joint written statement and defendant Nos.27-29 filed another written statement. The case of the defendant Nos.2, 3 and 6 is that Nasaruddin died leaving behind his son Hamijuddin and one daughter Sarbanu @ Sawrupjan Bibi and wife Arabjan who inherited his share. Hamijuddin inherited his share and his, daughter Sawraupjan inherited 4 annas share and his first wife Arabjan Bibi got 2 annas share. Sawrupjan Bibi was given in marriage with Babar Mollah and they had two sons and one daughter in the wedlock. After the death of Babar Mollah, Sawrupjan Bibi was again married to Ludu Mollah and after the death of Sawrupjan her property was inherited by her daughter Samarthaban Bibi and her husband Ludu Mollah and mother Arabjan Bibi. Two sons of Swarupjan Bibi died unmarried. Arabjan Bibi transferred her share to the predecessor of these defendants on 13th Boishakh, 1319 B.S. by Heba deed and afterwards she sold her land inherited from her daughter to Hamijuddin by another deed. Thereafter Somarthaban Bibi and Ludu Mollah sold 9 gonda 2 kranti share on 23.12.1920 to the predecessor of the defendant and delivered possession. At the time of preparation of S.A. record the same was correctly prepared in their names. 

 5. The learned Assistant Judge on consideration of the materials on record decreed the suit in part holding that Ext.6=Ext. Kha was executed only by Ludu Molla and not by Samarthaban Bibi and as such her property was not transferred by this document. The defendants then preferred Title Appeal No.2 of 1996 and the court of appeal allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit holding that Somorthaban Bibi duly executed Ext.6=Ext. Kha and as such her share was duly transferred by this document. The plaintiff then preferred the above mentioned civil revisional application and the Rule was discharged.

full_judgment:
2. The relevant facts, for disposal of this appeal, in short, are that the land measuring an area of 15.20 acres in C.S khatian No. 122, 252, 255 and 817 of Mouja Chalita Bunia under Police Station Morrelganj owned by two brothers namely, Serajuddin and Daliluddin in equal shares. Serajuddin died leaving two sons, the defenant Nos. 13 and 14 and Daliluddin died leaving four sons, the plaintiffs, the defendant No.1 Abdul Gani and Abdul Aziz. Serajuddin and Daliluddin decided to transfer the suit land by way of gift to their sons. At the time the plaintiffs were minors. The suit land was recorded in the names of their two brothers Abdul Aziz and Abdul Gani Daliluddin and Serajuddin eecuted two different transfer deeds on 14m June, 1937 and 30th June, 1937 to their sons in respect of 15.20 acres. On the basis of those deeds, the defendant Nos. 13 and 14 have been possessing their shares. The plaintiffs have been living in different houses. On 5tn September, 1980 Anwar Hossain, defendant No. 2 disclosed that S.A. record-of-rights was not prepared in the plaintiffs' names, which clouded their title in the suit land. Hence, was the suit. 

 4. Specific case of the defendants was that Daliluddin and Serajuddin transferred a portion of the suit land of C.S. khatian No. 817 to Abdul Aziz, defendant Nos. 1 and 13 to 14 by a sale deed dated 14.06.1937 and gifted the rest land to them from the remaining 3 khatians by a deed of gift dated 30.06.1937. The suit should be dismissed. 

 6. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the appellants, submits that the plaintiffs sought for declaration of title in respect of 3.80 acres of land out of 15.20 acre in four khatians without giving specific boundary of the said land. He further submits that the suit itself was no maintainable without seeking relief for cancellation of the deeds inasmuch as admittedly, the suit property to defendant No.1, Abdul Aziz, predecessor-in-interest of defendants No.2-12 and the defendants No. 13 and 14 by two separate registered transfer deeds dated 14m and 30m June, 1937 but the plaintiffs did not seek any relief by way of cancellation of those deeds. He further submits that the suit itself was hopelessly barred by limitation, this Division as well as the High Court Division failed to consider the point of limitation thereby, erroneously decreed the suit. 

 7. Admittedly, one Daliluddin and Serajuddin were the original owners of the land measuring an area 15.20 acres of C. S khatian No. 122, 252, 255 and 817. Serajuddin died leaving two sons, the defendant No. 13 and 14. On the other hand Daliluddin died leaving behind plaintiffs, defendant No. 1 Abdul Gani and Abdl Aziz, predecessor-in-interest of the defendant No. 2 to 12. The plaintiffs claimed their title in respect of 3.80 acres of land as two sons of Daliluddin. 

 8. The plaintiffs claimed title to 3.80 acres of land from CS khatinas no 122, 252, 255 and 817 but the schedule to the plaint describes only the lands of three CS khatians namely CS Khatian no 122, 252 and 255. There is no description of land which they claim from CS khatian no 817. In a suit for declaration of title there shall be proper identification of land as per Order 7 Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Neither the courts below nor the High Court Division noticed the above-mentioned anomaly in the schedule of the plaint. The Appellate Court categorically stated that upon perusal of exhibit No. "জ" it appeared that Daliluddin Howlader was literate and he could sign but it appeared from the solenama that Daliluuddin Howlader put his thumb impression there-in which clearly established the fact that Daliluddin Howlader did not compromise the suit with the plaintiffs through solenama. But one of the grounds for setting aside the judgments of the Appellate Court by the High Court Division was the com-promise of the suit by the defendant No 1 and 15 (Daliluddin) with the plaintiff by solanama. The High Court Division did not reverse the findings of the Appellate Court that Daliluddin was literate and, therefore, his thumb impression on the solename made the same highly doubtful.

full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that A. Gofur was tenant under Ray Bihari Lal Bahadur represented by Administrator General of Bengal. Due to arrear of rent landlord filed Rent Suit 1941 of 1940 and got decree and the suit land was sold in Rent Execution Case 622 of 1943 and auction was purchased by Hachen Uddin on 9-11- 1943 and got possession on 14-3-1944. It is further stated that another Rent Suit 1927 of 1948 was subsequently filed and the suit land was again sold in Rent Execution Case 404 of 1949 and auction was purchased by Gogon Ali and Mofizuddin Howlader on 31-5-1949 which was confirmed on 14-4-1949 and later on possession was delivered. Auction purchasers settled the suit land with the predecessors of the plaintiffs named Rahman Faraji, Kader Faraji, Abdul Hakim, Gani Faraji, Abdul Motaleb, Abdul Khaleque, Muslemuddin and Tofayel Ahmed at an annual rental of 50 taka 6 anna and accordingly RS record 487 was prepared in their names. Gani, Motaleb, Khaleque possessed 8 annas share wherefrom they sold 0.304 acres to plaintiff 1 and Erfan by kabala dated 24-3-1955. Erfan sold 0.16 acres to plaintiff 4 and 0.16 acres to plaintiff 2 and 3 by two kabalas dated 21-4-1983. Rahman executed a patta in respect of 0.32 acres of land on 5-6-1950 to Mofizuddin who sold the same to Erfan, Hachen, Azhar by kabala dated 3-4-1956. Erfan transferred his share to plaintiffs 2 and 3. Azhar made an oral gift of his share to grandson plaintiff 2. It is also stated that one Tofazzal sold by kabala dated 12-4-1949 to Ibrahim who sold 0.63 acres to Erfan and plaintiff 1 through kabala dated 14-11-1955. Erfan orally gifted his share to plaintiff 2. Tofayel transferred 0.81 acres of land in favour of Sultan, Lehaj Uddin, Anwara through kabala 2976 dated 23-10-1956. Sultan died leaving behind plaintiffs 10, 11 and 12. Lehaj Uddin was the predecessor of plaintiffs 13-18. Anwara died and her heirs sold the land to plaintiff 2. Tofayel also sold 0.32 acres to plaintiff 1 through kabala dated 7-3-1955. Plaintiff 1 sold 0.08 acres to plaintiff 20 on 12-6-2007. Thus plaintiffs acquired 5.44 acres of land as mentioned in schedule `Kha'. The RS and SA record were correctly prepared jointly with the predecessor of the defendants. Due to inconvenience in possession plaintiff asked defendants for partition but they did not pay any heed to it and refused the same on 2nd Boishakh, 1411 BS. Hence the suit was filed. 

 4. Defendants 1-6 appeared and contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying all material statements made in the plaint contending inter alia that the suit is barred by limitation and also under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. It was further stated that Rashid, Hachen, Tachen, Samed, Rafizuddin, Atabar were owners in possession and they settled 9.77 acres of land at a yearly rental of 50 taka 6 anna to Abdur Rahman Faraji by registered dakhila dated 1-3-1946 but his brothers' names were wrongly inserted in RS khatian 487 along with his name. Rahman died leaving behind daughter Kulsum, wives Shamsunnessa and Rahima, sons defendants 1-6 named Rob, Sobhan, Huq, Wahid, Barek, Awal. Sons and mothers filed Title Suit 166 of 1978 on 26-4-1978 for declaration of title against the wrong record. Suit was renumbered as 389 of 1981 and 126 of 1983. Defendants 6(Ka)/6(Ga)/15-17/18(Ka)-18(Kha) /20(Ka) and plaintiffs filed compromise petition in the suit and accordingly suit was decreed on 4-4-1985 and title of Rahman's heirs was declared. Later on defendant 12 of that suit named Fulboru filed Miscellaneous Case 34 of 1985 which was allowed on 30-7-1988. Present defendants then preferred Civil Revision 186 of 1988 in the then Barishal Bench of this Division which was transferred to Dhaka High Court and renumbered as Civil Revision 10205 of 1991. Sufia is the wife of Lehaj Uddin and mother of present plaintiffs 13-18. She died and her heirs executed a deed of relinquishment on 5-5-1991 and admitted title of the present defendants. Accordingly parties entered into compromise on 5-3-1998 which was allowed and the decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 remained intact and the Rule was made absolute on 25-3-1998. The case of the plaintiffs is false. Predecessor of plaintiffs 6-10 named Hachen also registered a nadabi dated 5-6-1995 admitting the title and possession of the present defendants. Hachen Ali is still alive. Meanwhile present defendants filed GR Case 31 of 1998 in which the statement of Title Suit 126 of 1983 was given. Earlier Hachen filed Miscellaneous Petition Case 213 of 1991 in which possession was found in favour of these appellant-defendants. Plaintiffs have definite knowledge of earlier Title Suit 126 of 1983. Present defendants have been maintaining title and possession in the suit land by living in their homestead and through cultivation upon payment of rent. Son of plaintiff 3 recently purchased from the defendants on 1-4-2003 admitting the decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983. The suit being false is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 7. The Joint District Judge decreed the suit in part by judgment and decree dated 3-6-2008 on the finding that defendants could not offer satisfactory answer against the correctness of record of rights and records were correctly prepared and plaintiffs have acquired 3.92 acres of land through transfers and the nadabi document as claimed by defendants do not confer title and DW 1 admitted that there is only one plaintiff who was party to earlier suit thus the impugned decree is not binding upon the rest 19 plaintiffs and since plaintiffs have title in the instant suit land the decree of Title Suit 126 of 1983 passed in favour of defendants becomes inoperative. 

 9. Mr Swapon Kumar Dutta, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the plaintiffs did not make out any case as to why the decree of `Ga' schedule is fraudulent and not binding upon them and plaintiffs cannot escape from discharging such heavy onus which squarely lies upon them. RS record was wrongly prepared in the names of all sons of Sonamuddi Faraji for which settlement holder Rahman's heirs filed Title Suit 166 of 1978 renumbered as 126 of 1983 for declaration of title against such wrong record impleading other sons of Sonamuddi or their heirs and got their title declared which was affirmed by this Division in Civil Revision 10205 of 1991 on 25-3-1998. That judgment was not challenged and examined by our Appellate Division and this suit was filed after 06(six) years on 19-6-2004. On the strength of such decree defendants have mutated their names and have been maintaining title and possession in the suit land upon payment of rent. Plaintiffs are never their co-sharers and this suit being false is liable to be dismissed outright. He further submits that the deeds of relinquishment executed by the then defendants in the suit and revision although do not confer title but those are strong admissions and the present plaintiffs are now estopped from denying the title of the appellants. He then submits that Title Suit 126 of 1983 was mentioned in Criminal PS Case 04 of 1986 and after a long lapse of time the instant suit for declaration against the 'Ga' schedule decree dated 4-4-1985 is barred by limitation. He then referring to `Ga' schedule decree strongly submits that the heirs of some of the defendants of earlier suit along with others filed the instant suit thus this suit suffers multifariousness because parties to earlier suit although does not require declaration of title but the rest requires such relief thus their claim is vague and suit cannot run in accordance with law. In furtherance of such submission he proceeds that the rest defendants of earlier suit who did not file the instant suit must be made defendants to protect their valuable rights but the same having been not done the instant suit suffers defect of party. He finally submits that the Joint District Judge misquoted the evidence of DW 1 and arrived at a wrong conclusion. In support of his submission he refers the cases of Subitri Bari vs Assistant Custodian of Enemy Property and other; 39 DLR 172; Rezaul Karim and others vs Shamsuzzoha and others, 49 DLR (AD) 68; Abu Naser Mohd. Wahidun Nabi and another vs Balai Roy and others, 10 MLR (AD) 121; Akitullah and others vs Zafala Begum and others, 54 DLR (AD) 74 and prays for allowing the appeal. 

 10. Mr Sarder Abul Hossain, learned Advocate on the other hand appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that the Joint District Judge upon proper appreciation of evidence has rightly passed the judgment. He draws our attention to RS record 487 and submits that the RS record has got its presumptive value and defendants could not dislodge such presumption by any convincing evidence. The Joint District Judge upon perusal of Exhibits-3-9 has correctly found that the plaintiffs are entitled to a decree in part which may not be interfered with by this Court. The claim of the defendants relying upon two nadabi documents does not deserve any consideration because those do not confer any title. He laid much emphasis on the statement of DW 1 made in cross and submits that according to the admission of DW 1 the decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 is not binding upon the plaintiffs and plaintiffs have been maintaining title and possession in the suit land. He referring to the deposition of DW 1 submits that the Joint District Judge has passed the judgment upon due consideration of materials on record and the appeal is liable to be dismissed. In course of hearing Mr Hossain filed an application for amendment of the plaint on 15-3-2023 and on 30-3-2023 filed another application for production of additional evidence. In support of those applications he submits that at the time of hearing of this appeal plaintiffs have come to know some important facts and documents with regard to their title which are very much necessary for proper adjudication of the dispute and unless those are considered and allowed the respondents shall suffer irreparable loss and injury. 

 11. We have heard the learned Advocates and examined all the materials on record and also gone through the impugned judgment as well as the grounds taken in appeal. 

 12. From reading of paragraph 2 of the plaint it appears that plaintiffs cited two auction issues. First auction was purchased by Hachen Uddin and the second one was by Gogon Ali and Mafizuddin. Plaintiffs claim their title through settlement from Gogon and Mafizuddin on the other hand defendants claim their title through settlement from Hachen Talukder and others. Plaintiffs claim that according to the settlement RS record 487 Exhibit-IX was correctly prepared in the names of six sons of Sonamuddi Faraji named Rahman, Kader, Hakim, Gani, Motaleb, Khaleque Rahman is the predecessor of contesting defendants 1-6. Plaintiffs did not produce any document of title showing settlement in their favour nor did they bother to mention the date of taking such settlement. Plaintiffs also did not produce the suit registers of those two rent suits despite availability of such documents in the concerned office. From reading of Exhibits-Kha and Kha(1) which are judgment and decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 it appears that the dispute arose in 1978 when defendants filed Title Suit 166 of 1978 subsequently renumbered as Title Suit 126 of 1983 for declaration of title against wrong entry in RS khatian 487 Exhibit-IX. In that suit the present defendants were plaintiffs and claimed that their father Rahman took settlement from Hachen and others by a registered dakhila dated 1-3-1946 Exhibit-Ka at an annual rental of 50 taka 6 anna but Rahman's brother named Gani managed to procure such wrong- record Exhibit-IX in collusion with the survey employees by dishonest means and out of greed. That suit was decreed on compromise against defendants 6(Ka)- 6(Ga)/15-17/18(Ka)-18(Gha)/20(Ka) and ex-parte against the rest. Defendants 15-18 of the earlier suit are RS tenants and consenting parties. The non-contesting defendant 12 named Fulbaru filed. Miscellaneous Case 34 of 1985 which was allowed on 30-7-1988. Present defendants filed Civil Revision 186 of 1988 which was subsequently renumbered as Civil Revision 10205 of 1991 wherein the heirs of deceased defendant 13 Lehajuddin executed a registered deed of relinquishment on 5-5-1991 Exhibit-Uma and admitted the title of the present defendants. The heirs of deceased Lehajuddin are plaintiffs 13-18 in this suit. Hachen who is the predecessor of plaintiffs 6-10 also admitted title and possession of the present defendants and executed a deed of relinquishment dated 5-6-1995 Exhibit-Cha. Subsequently heirs of deceased Fulbaru filed compromise with present defendants and admitted their title and possession in the suit land and accordingly Rule was made absolute on 25-3-1998 in Civil Revision 10205 of 1991 as apparent from Exhibits-Ga and Gha. Furthermore present defendants ailed GR Case 31 of 1998 in which the statement of Title Suit 126 of 1983 was given and the order sheet of GR Case is Exhibit-Chha. There is no reason to believe that the present plaintiffs had no knowledge of the earlier Title Suit 126 of 1983. 

 14. Second is the question of limitation. The `Ga' schedule decree was challenged after 19(nineteen) years. The judgment and decree was passed in Title Suit 126 of 1986 on 9-4-1985 Exhibit-'Kha series'. The instant suit challenging that decree was filed on 19-6-2004. The judgment of Civil Revision 10205 of 1991 was passed on 25-3-1998 Exhibits-Ga and Gha. There is sufficient and satisfactory evidence available in the instant case to decide the question of limitation although no issue on such point was framed by the trial Court despite its legal inevitability and necessity in order to reach to a satisfactory conclusion. This Court finds no reason to send the suit down on remand for framing an issue on question of limitation thereby shirk its responsibility. This Court has ample co-extensive power as like as the trial Court to question whether the suit is barred by limitation by framing an issue naming the same as issue No. 7 and disposing of the same under Section 107(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure when sufficient evidence are obtainable from the record to the satisfaction of the Court. The predecessor of plaintiffs 6-10 and 13-18 were defendants in Title Suit 126 of 1983 and they executed two deeds of relinquishment dated 5-6-1995 Exhibit-Cha and 5-5-1991 Exhibit-Uma and according to compromise the Rule was made absolute on 25-3-1998 and both Exhibits-Uma and Cha remained unchallenged in the instant suit although the executants are the plaintiffs in the suit. Thus it evidently transpires to us that plaintiffs have every knowledge of Exhibit-Kha series with Ga and Gha but they have challenged the decree after the statutory period of time. If it were argued that knowledge of some of the plaintiffs is not the knowledge of others in that case the suit fails on ground of multifariousness. Therefore issue No. 7 as framed by this Court goes against the case of the plaintiffs. 

 15. Third is that the suit was decreed in part relying on the denial part of DW 1. We paid our keen attention and went through the entire deposition of DW 1. From reading of the decree of Title Suit 126 of 1983 Exhibit-Kha(1) it is apparent that present plaintiffs 5, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18 along with others were defendants in Title Suit 126 of 1983. Thus it appears that while recording the deposition of DW 1 the word "not a fact" was mistakenly omitted from some places at the time of taking denial part by the presiding Judge. It becomes evidently clear when DW 1 immediately denied the suggestion at the end of his deposition as he stated that it was not a fact that plaintiffs possessed the suit land. Thus the finding of the Joint District Judge that since DW 1 admitted that there was only one defendant who is now the plaintiff and since the other plaintiffs were not parties the decree is not binding is abjectly perverse and misconceived and against documentary evidence. The lower Court failed to apply its judicial mind and did not even notice Exhibit-Kha(1) showing names and numbers of defendants of Title Suit 126 of 1983 and compare the same with the present plaint. The lower Court also went against the settled principle of law that plaintiff has to prove his own case independent of defence weakness. 

 16. Now we are going to consider the title of the parties. Plaintiff 14 who was one of the executants of Exhibit-Uma dated 5-5-1991 has deposed as PW 1. Although Exhibit-Uma is a deed of relinquishment and the same does not confer title but it is a registered document of admission and since no relief was prayed against Exhibits-Uma and Cha the documents stand good and plaintiff 14 is bound by such admission made in Exhibit-Uma and he is estopped from denying such admission thus the value of his testimony is greatly diminished. PW 2 and PW 3 deposed on possession and PW 3 failed to corroborate PW 2 as he admitted in cross that the land of Abdur Rahman is enjoyed by his sons. However since this is mainly a suit for partition evidence on possession does not carry much value except title. Plaintiffs claim title through settlement from auction purchasers Gogon and Mofijuddin. But they did not file any document of such settlement. It was not also explained away by them as to why they could not put forth such document. The document of title of the defendants for the selfsame land has been validated in Title Suit 126 of 1983 and Civil Revision 10205 of 1991. Defendants claim title through settlement from Hachen and others by registered dakhila Exhibit-Ka dated 1-3-1946. It appears from the pleadings and evidence that plaintiffs have relied on RS record 487 Exhibit-IX as the basis of their claim. Record of right is not a document of title. Moreover this Exhibit-IX has lost its value' by virtue of the decree passed in Title Suit 126 of 1983 and the judgment passed by this Division in Civil Revision 10205 of 1991. Defendants on the strength of decree mutated their names by Exhibit-Jha series and have been maintaining possession upon payment of rent Exhibit-Jha series. Earlier respondents filed three applications for amendment of the plaint and for taking additional evidence along with a supplementary affidavit but according to the order dated 30-11-2017 passed by a bench of this Court respondents did not press those applications at the time of hearing. So those applications are rejected being not pressed. Respondents also filed another application for amendment of the plaint on 15-3-2023 and also for acceptance of additional evidence on 30-3-2023 and those applications were heard. In the amendment of plaint respondents have made out a new case of kabuliyat and dakhila and in its support filed certified copies of kabuliyat and dakhila through application for acceptance of additional evidence. We have carefully examined those two documents and it appears that the kabuliyat dated 17-8-1944 was accepted by Hachen and others and they granted a dakhila on the same day to Rahman and his brothers. The second auction as drawn in the original plaint has been disowned in this amendment. Earlier plaintiffs claimed through Gogon and Mofijuddin and the rent was 50 taka 6 anna and quantum of the holding was 9.72 acres according to schedule-Ka. Now they are claiming through Hachen and others and the joma is 44 taka 8 anna and quantum of joma is 8.75 acres which is inconsistent with schedule-Ka. The dakhila shows that education cess is fixed at 2 taka 4 anna which actually was not imposed at the time in 1351 BS as found our Appellate Division in the case of Joynal Abedin Molla vs Aliyar Rahman and others, 1983 BLD (AD) 105. Plaintiffs were acquainted with Exhibit-Ka dated 1-3-1946 since 1978 when Title Suit 166 of 1978 renumbered as Title Suit 126 of 1983 was filed. That document stands good in the suit and revision Exhibit-Kha series, Ga and Gha. Now after around 26(twenty-six) years plaintiffs have come forward with those applications in view to fill up their lacuna by making out a new case on their acquisition of title to the surprise of the other party. The other party cannot be taken by surprise specially when a valuable right is accrued in their favour by lapse of time. Had Exhibit-Kha series been found fraudulent according to pleading and evidence in that case these proposed applications would have been taken in adjudication. It also calls for our attention that in Title Suit 126 of 1983 the RS tenants Gani Faraji, Abul Khaleque, Tofayel Ahmed admitting the title of Rahman Faraji which he acquired through Exhibit-Ka entered into compromise which was not denied in revision Exhibits-Ga and Gha. Court has to follow the principles of law and we have no option but to reject those applications filed after such a belated stage. It has also come to our notice that in paragraph 2 of the application for production of additional evidence it is admitted that the original kabulyat was under the custody of executant Abdur Rahman Faraji thus it appears that the same was not acted upon being not accepted by the landlord. 

 18. The lower Court found that defendants could not make any satisfactory reply against the SA record. He did not even bother to notice the SA and RS record distinctively. Court failed to appreciate that the satisfactory reply against the record of right was Exhibits-Ka and Kha series along with Ga and Gha. The Court abruptly found the SA and RS record are correct without assigning any reason and also miscalculated the quantum of land of 3.92 acres in granting the part decree without showing any reason as to why the remaining land could not be given. The lower Court misconceived the law and facts of the case and arrived at a wrong conclusion. Plaintiffs have failed to prove their own case and it appears that plaintiffs out of greed have filed this suit if the land or portion of it could be consumed in any way. They did not file any cross appeal for the rest 1.52 acres. The claim of the plaintiffs is absolutely false. 

 Communicate this judgment and send down the lower Court's record.

lawyer:
Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, Senior Advocate with NK Saha, Senior Advocate, instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record—For the Appellants.

VS

full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique, CJ: The appellants filed Title Suit No.21 of 2000 in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Narayangonj for declaration of title in respect of the suit described in the schedule to the plaint stating, inter alia, that one Chandra Mohon Pal and Modon Mohon Pal were the CS recorded tenants having 0.55 acre of -land of CS plot No.12 appertaining to CS khatian No.17 of Mouza Alinagar under Police Station-Fatullah, District Narayangonj. Chandra Mohon Pal died leaving behind one daughter, plaintiff No.1 who inherited 8 annas shares of the suit land. Modon Mohon Pal also died leaving behind his daughter Sattya Bala Pal who married with one Ramani Mohon Pal. Sattya Bala Pal died leaving behind 6 sons including plaintiff Nos.2 and 3 who inherited the remaining portion of the suit property. During SA operation their names had been duly recorded in SA khatian. One of the sons of Sattya Bala Pal, namely, Chitta Ranjan Pal died and whereabouts of 3 other sons were not known. The plaintiff Nos.2-3 had been owning and possessing the respective shares of their brothers including their own shares of the suit property. Suit land was residential plot of the plaintiffs which had been let out to other persons on rent for bricks and stones business. They had paid rents and taxes to the government upto 1392 BS. After the war of liberation, the plaintiffs have .been residing at their present addresses in Jamalpur and Narayangonj. Due to absence of the plaintiffs, the suit land had been wrongly recorded in RS khatian No.4 in the name of the government. The government mutated the suit land in the name of M/s Elahi Buksh Cold Storage and Company Limited (in short, the Company) represented by the Ministry of Commerce, the Government of Bangladesh in Mutation Case No.4884 of 1991. Cause of action of the suit arose on 2-1-2000 when the plaintiffs went to the concerned office for payment of rent and came to know about the said wrong record of right. So, they instituted the present suit. 

 2. The defendant Nos.1-3 and 5-6 contested the suit by filing separate sets of written statements. The defendant Nos.1-3 contended that the suit land being abandoned property had been recorded in RS khatian No.4 during the last revisional survey operation and was amalgamated with other plots of Elahi Buksh Cold Storage & Company Limited measuring 1.92 acres of land in the name of the Ministry of Commerce, Government of Bangladesh in Miscellaneous Case No.7/85 (AP) dated 5-12-1985. The Company had paid land development Tax upto 1405 BS. The plaintiffs, forging some documents, instituted the present suit with a view to grab the government property. 

 3. The contentions of the defendant Nos.5 and 6 in short, are that the suit land measuring 55 decimals were recorded in the names of the plaintiffs and others in SA khatian No.21, SA Plot No-12- Plaintiff No.1, Taru Bala Pal sold 0.14 acre of land from suit plot to the defendant Nos.5 and 6, the Company by registered sale deed No.5323 dated 29-9-62. Rukkoni Bala and others sold 0.16 acre of land of suit plot by registered sale deed No.6807 dated 6-12-62 to the company. Mohon Razbonshi sold out 0.12 acre of land by registered deed No.731 dated 25-1-1963 to the Company. Aeson Company Limited, by deed No.4401 dated 12-6-1999, exchanged 14 decimals of land with the Company. The defendant no.5, while enjoying the possession of the suit land, established a cold storage therein. During the war of liberation the original owenrs of the company left the country. Accordingly, vide SET Miscellaneous Case No.7/85(AP) dated 5-12-85 the suit properties had been declared as abandoned property and it was ultimately vested in the government. Its management had been controlled by the Board of management duly constituted by Ministry of Commerce. During RS survey the suit property had been duly recorded in the name of the Government of Bangladesh represented by the Ministry of Commerce. The said khatian had been amalgamated with other properties of the company measuring 1.92 acres of land and was finally published in RS khatian No.4. The plaintiff never possessed the suit land and that the instant suit had been instituted by the plaintiffs in order to grab the government property with some fictitious documents. The suit was liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 6. Mr Amit Das Gupta, learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the respondent Government, submits that the High Court Division upon proper appreciation of the materials on record, held that the instant suit was not maintainable. He submits that the plaintiffs have failed to prove their title and possession in the entire suit land, the High Court Division rightly dismissed the suit. 

 7. Admittedly, the suit land originally belonged to Chandra Mohon Pal and Madon Mohon Pal to the extent of 8 annas share each. Chandra Mohon Pal died leaving only daughter, Taru Bala Pat, the plaintiff No.1. On the other hand, Modon Mohon Pal died leaving daughter Sattya Bala Pal. Sattya Bala Pal died leaving 6(six) sons, namely, Chitta Ranjan Pal, Monoranjan Pal, Shishu Ranjan Pal, Khushi Ranjan Pal, Nidhon Ranjan Pal and Aurun Ranjan Pal. Khusi Ranjan Pal, Nidon Ranjan and Aurun Ranjan Pal were untraced since 1971 and their interest was ultimately devolved to their brothers Monoronjan Pal and Shishu Ranjan Pal, the plaintiff No.2 and 3. SA record-of-rights was prepared in their names. 

 8. It was the case of the contesting defendants that Taru Bala and others transferred 0.14 acre of land on 29-9-1962, Rukkhini Bala and others transferred their 0.16 acre of land on 6-12-1962 and Mohon Rajbonshi transferred 0.12 acre of land on 25-1-1963 to M/s Elahi Boksh and Company Limited. From the materials on record, it appears that the plaintiffs are the successive heirs of CS recorded tenants and their names were duly recorded in SA khatian. The contesting defendants relied upon 3(three) kabala deeds. Of them, kabla deed dated 6-12-1962 in respect of 0.16 acre of land was executed by Rukkhini Bala and others and kabala deed dated 25-1-1963 in respect of 0.12 acre of land was executed by Mohon Rajbongshi. The defendants hopelessly failed to prove the source of title of Rukkhini Bala and Mohon Rajbongshi. In absence of any proof of source of title of the executants of those deeds, it is difficult to hold that the defendants had acquired any title on the basis of deeds dated 6-12-1962 and 25-1-1963. The learned Advocate appearing for the respondents also failed to satisfy us as to the source of their title. In such view of the matter, it is difficult to hold that by those deeds, the contesting defendants have acquired any title in the suit land. In such circumstances, we have no hesitation to hold that the plaintiffs' title in the suit land remained undisturbed. The Court of facts below concurrently disbelieved the execution and registration of the said deeds.

2. The present lave petitioner and pro-forma respondent Nos. 51-54 herein, as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.71 of 2003 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Hajiganj Chandpur for declaration of title and partition claiming separate shaham for .75 acre of land. The material case of the plaintiffs, in short, was that Abbas Ali was the owner of five anna six ganda two kara two kranti share of the land of C.S. Khatian No.71 of Mouza-Motani of Upazila Hajigonj, under District-Chandpur. The said Abbas Ali died before C.S. operation leaving behind two sons and three daughters namely Bande Ali, Akrammudin, Alekjan Bibi, Elemjan Bibi and Sabjan Bibi. That during C.S. operation, Bande Ali and Akramuddin fraudulently did not record the names of their sisters in C.S. record of rights. That Elemjan Bibi became widow with one son and three daughters namely Muslim Uddin, Meherunnessa, Ulfatenessa and Arabennessa and she was then taken by her brother Akramuddin to their paternal home and since then Elemjan Bibi was residing in her paternal home by erecting a dwelling house thereon. That Muslim Uddin died before Elemjan leaving behind only son Anwarullah. Elemjan orally gifted 1.28 acres of land in favour of the son Anwar Ullah and delivered possession of the same. That Arabennessa, the daughter of Elemjan died leaving one son and two daughters namely Aynuddin, Eannatunnesa and Henzil Begum. That daughters of Elemjan namely, Meherannessa and Ulfatunnessa admitted the ownership of Anwar Ullah by mutating a registered "Muktipatra" dated 17.02.1954. That Anwar Ullah transferred 27 decimals of land and the rest 1.01 acres of land has been mutated in his name in Kharize Khatian No.75 and he possessed the same on payment of rent. Those lands have been recorded in the name of Anwar Ullah in B.S. Khatian also. That Anwar Ullah possessed 37 decimals of land from the estern part of Plot No.4 and transferred that in favour of the plaintiffs vide kabala dated 28.05.1995 and also delivered possession of the same in favour of the plaintiffs. That the plaintiffs have been possessing that land by erecting dwelling house therein. That .03 decimals of land of the plaintiffs has been attracted in the care road and rest 34 decimals of land are under possession of the plaintiffs from the eastern side of Plot No.4. That A. Khaleque, A Malek and Mafia Khatun the other co-sharers of the suit holding exchanged their land to the plaintiffs vide exchange deed dated 12.08.1999 and thus the plaintiffs are owner of total 71 decimals of land of Plot No.4 and 4 decimals of land of Plot No. 39. The defendant No.1 intended to purchase 37 decimals of land of Plot No.4 from Anwar Ullah but he did not agree. That the defendant No.1 with the aid and assistance of Bande Ali Mia filed appeal under Section 31 of the Bengal Tenancy Rules against the record of the plaintiffs and also created an antedated Bainapatra and instituted Title Suit No. 41 of 2000 before the Assistant Judge, Hajigonj, Chandrapur and knowing about that suit, the plaintiffs filed application for addition of party in that suit which was ultimately allowed. Against that order the defendant No.1 filed Civil Revision before the High Court Division which was allowed and the order of addition of party was set aside. Later the said Title Suit No.41 of 2000 was dismissed ex-parte. Against that judgment and decree the defendant No.1 preferred appeal being Title Appeal No.157 of 2001 which was ultimately allowed ex-parte. The plaintiffs then instituted Title Suit No.59 of 2000 for permanent injunction which was decreed. The defendant No.1 preferred Title Appeal No.68 of 2004 against that judgment and decree which was dismissed. This plaintiffs thus are possessing their land peacefully. Since there was no partition by metes and bounds and boundary dispute arose among the co-sharers the plaintiffs were constrained to file this suit. 

 3. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filling written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending inter alia that 2.03 acres of land of C.S. Khatian No.71 has been recorded correctly in the name of settlement holders Akramuddin, Bande Ali and Meher Ali. That Meher Ali being owner of .3383 acre of land died leaving behind two sons and one daughter namely Nowab Ali, Munsur Ali and Ful Banu. Ful Banu orally gifted her share in favour of two brothers. Nowab Ali died leaving 3 sons and 2 daughters namely Fazlul Haque (defendant No.1), Sirajul Haque, Shamsul Haque, Fatema Begum and Latifa Begum. Through amicable partition among them, Shamsul Haque got .115 acres of land and defendant No.1 got .0541 acres of land. That the defendant No. I purchased .115 acre of land from Shamsul Haque and became owner of .01692 acre of land. That Munsur Ali died leaving 3 sons and a daughter namely, Ishaque, A Momin, Syedur Rahman and Zulekha Khatun. The defendant No.1 purchased .115 acre from them. That the heirs of Bande Ali namely Khaliqur Rahman and others agreed to sell .2963 acres of land from Plot No.4 and executed a Bainaptra but they did not execute and register the kabala in favour of the defendant No.1 and the defendant No. 1 therefore, filed Title suit No.51 of 2000 for specific performance of contract which was dismissed by the trial Court and the defendant No.1 then preferred Title Appeal No.157 of 2001 and obtained a decree in that suit. The defendant No.1 became owner of .5801 acre of land of C.S. Khatian No.71. That Abbas Ali was not the owner of the C.S. Khatian as claimed by the plaintiffs. It was the self-acquired properties of Bande Ali and Akramuddin and accordingly recorded in C.S. Khatian in their names and as such the name of 3 daughters of Abbas Uddin was not recorded in C.S. Khatian. That Elemjan had no share and she had no transferable interest. That the title of Elemjan is clouded by the C.S. record and as such the plaintiffs were to pray for declaration of title also the present suit is not maintainable in its form; that Anwar Ullah could not become the owner of any land by dint of oral gift made by Elemjan and the plaintiffs being purchaser from Anwar Ullah could not acquire any right, title in the suit land. 

 6. The plaintiffs-appellants then preferred the above mentioned civil revision before the High Court Division and obtained Rule. Ultimately a Single Bench of the High Court Division made that Rule absolute in part setting aside the judgment and decree of the appellate Court below and restoring those of the trial Court. The High Court Division on examination of the evidence on record found that both the Courts below rightly found that Anwar Ullah could not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit land by virtue of the alleged oral gift from Elemjan and that Elemjan Bibi had no right and title in those land. The High Court Division found also that the contesting defendants did not raise any objection against the claim of the plaintiffs in other 37 decimals of land which they claimed to have acquired by dint of registered exchange deed dated 12.08.1999, the Ext. 9 from other co-sharers and in the circumstances the trial Court rightly allotted this quantum of land in the share of the plaintiffs, but the appellate Court below unnecessarily discussed this point with some wrong observations. The High Court Division found that the findings and decision of the appellate Court below so far as it relate to the plaintiffs' exchange deed dated 12.08.1999, the Ext.-9 were erroneous and as such were liable to be set aside.

full_judgment:
2. Facts of the case, in brief, are that the respondent as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No 13 of 1984 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sujanagar, Pabna, for declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession of the Suit property measuring .20 acre of land under plot No. 633 appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 4, S.A. Khatian No. 275 of Mouja Sufanagar, stating, inter alia, that the suit property originally belonged to ex-landlord Tara Gobinda Chowdhury and others and they possessed the same as it was under their khas possession. Being approached by the Hindu Community for using the suit property as cremation ground, the ex-landlords approved their proposal and consequently allowed them to create a cremation ground thereon and, thereafter, the suit property has been used as cremation ground by the local Hindu Community and for the aforesaid reason an Ekrarnama dated 22.03.1947 was executed by the ex-landlords in respect of the suit property and its possession was delivered to the plaintiff committee and since then the plaintiff committee has been using the suit property as cremation ground for more than 12 years within the knowledge of all including the defendants. The ex-landlords never settled the suit property to anybody. The cremations on file suit property has been managed by the local Hindu Community through a committee and the plaintiff being Secretary of the committee instituted the above suit. S.A. record was wrongly prepared in the name of defendant No. 2. Defendant No. 1 being purchaser from defendant No. 2 claimed his title over the suit property in the month of Baishakh, 1983 and denied the title of the plaintiff. The plaintiff was not aware of the wrong S.A. record and deed of purchase of defendant No. 1. During S.A. survey, the Survey Officer told the plaintiff that the suit land would be recorded as Government khan land showing possession of the Committee with remarks for public use. Subsequently, defendant No. 3 son of defendant No. 1 in the year 1982 dispossessed the plaintiff and an allegation was filed before the S.D.O. Sadar, Pabna. Hence, the plaintiff Committee represented by its Secretary filed the suit. 

 3. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit property originally belonged to Khirod Gobinda Chowdhury, Tara Gobinda Chowdhury and Tarak Gobinda Chowdhury. Khirod Gobinda Chowdhury settled the suit property in favour of Dukhu Sheikh (defendant No.2), who on settlement got possession of the same on payment of rents to the ex-landlord. During S.A. operation, the suit property was recorded in the mime of the, ex-landlord Khirod Gobinda Chowdhury and Dukhu Sheikh filed Objection Case No. 26 of 1960 and got S.A. record in his name and, thereafter, Dukhu Sheikh transferred the suit property by registered deed dated 03.10.1962 in favour of defendant No. 1 and delivered possession in his favour. Defendant No. 1 mutated the suit property in his name and paid rent to the government. The plaintiff never acquired any title and possession to the suit land. During liberation war the patni papers of Dukhu Sheikh were lost and thus those could not be delivered in favour of defendant No. 1. 

 5. After hearing the parties and considering the evidence on record the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sujanagar, Pabna by his judgment and decree dated 11.04.2002 decreed the suit. 

 6. Against the said judgment and decree passed by the trial Court the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 93 of 2002 and upon hearing the parties and considering the materials on record the learned Special District Judge, Pabna allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

 9. Mrs. Sufia Khatun, learned Advocate-on-Record appearing for the respondents made submission in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. 

 10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned, perused the impugned judgment and other connected papers on record. 

 11. A perusal of the judgment of the appellate Court discloses that the evidence of the witnesses was not discussed whereas the trial Court observed that P.Ws. 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 consistently deposed that the suit land has been used as cremation ground. The trial Court further observed that defendant No. 2, who deposed as P.W.1, filed a solenama stating inter alia, that the suit land was never settled in his favour and that he did not execute any deed in favour of defendant No. 1 on 03.10.1962, but defendant No. 1 did not cross-examine hint to controvert his statement and deposition. The lower appellate Court, on the other hand, reversed the decree of the trial Court, upon relying on the deed of sale, executed by defendant No. 2 in the year 1962 and the consequent record of rights in favour of defendant No. 1. The appellate Court also relied upon the fact that the plaintiff committee neither took any step to record its name in the S.A. record nor paid any tax in respect of the suit land, nor produced any papers in respect of the use of the land as a cremation ground and thereby allowed the appeal. 

 13. The defendants did not produce any evidence with regard to the alleged settlement of the suit property in favour of Dukhu Sheikh by the Jamindar giving an explanation that the papers were lost during the liberation war. In the absence of such papers and in view of the positive evidence of defendant No. 2 Dukhu Sheikh that he did not get settlement of the suit property from the Jamindar, nor executed any deed in favour of defendant No. 1 in 1962, the High Court Division rightly excluded the evidence of D.W. 4; the Deed Writer. Moreover, the High Court Division observed that D.W. I himself, although alive at the time of trial and present in the Court did not depose in support of the defendants' case. The son of defendant No. 1, who deposed in Court merely stated that his father (defendant No. 1) was present in the Court, but unwell. However he did not produce any medical certificate in support. In this regard the High Court Division accepted the claim of the plaintiff that D. W. 1 did not depose because he would not wish to depose falsely. In our view the High Court Division correctly concluded that since the settlement in favour of Dukhu Sheikh does not stand, the S.A. record in his favour has no basis.

Salma Masud Choudhury J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the enlistment of the property of the petitioner to the extent of his share measuring 12 decimals of BS Plot No. 157 appertaining to BS Khatian No. 9 recorded in the name of predecessor of the petitioner/ transferor corresponding to PS Plot No. 99 of PS Khatian No. 52 transformed from RS Plot No. 87/104 as appeared in item No.98 mentioning Plot No.9, Mouza Pahartali under PS Double mooring at page-15656(Kha) published in the Bangladesh Gazette on 26-12-1988 vide SRO 378-Law dated 25-12-1988 purportedly made under section 5(1) of the Bangladesh Abandoned Building (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance 1985 should not be declared to have been done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. In the present Writ Petition the petitioner challenges the enlistment of his property appertaining to RS Khatian No.31, RS Plot No.87/104, PS Khatian No.52, PS Plot No.99, BS Khatian No.9, BS Plot No.157, JL, No.5, Mouza-Lot-9 Pahartali, Police Station-Double Moorings (Pahartali), District-Chittagong in the Kha(2) list as a supplementary to the Kha list of the abandoned properties published in the Bangladesh Gazette Extra-ordinary dated 26-12-1988 at page No.15656(Kha) against serial No.98 under the caption Plot No.9 Pahartali, Police Station-Double Moorings and the total area of 6.94 acres of land including the land in question appertaining to RS (CS) Khatian Nos.15 and 31 under Mouza Lot 9 Pahartali, JL No.5, Police Station- Double Moorings, District-Chittagong originally belonged to one Lalit Mohon Roy and others and in the RS (CS) operation the same was recorded in the names of one Amin Sharif and Serajul Haque as rayati tenants and thereafter the said Amin Sharif died leaving behind one daughter Sajeda Khatun as his sole heir and while enjoying and possessing the above land the said Sajeda Khatun transferred 1.12 acres of land including the land in question in favour of one Anwara Ahammad Chowdhury by a registered sale deed being No.2951 dated 16-4-1956 and delivered possession in favour of the transferee and was completely extinguished there from and after purchase, the said Anwara Ahammad Chowdhury, started enjoying and possessing the land peacefully within the knowledge of all and paid upto date land development tax to the government exchequer and during the BS operation, BS Khatian No.9 was correctly prepared and finally published in her name in 1987 and thereafter on 21-8-1994 at about 9-30 PM the said Anwara Ahammed Chowdhury died in Dhaka because of old age complications and during her life time Anwara Ahammed Chowdhury transferred the land in question measuring 12 decimals in favour of the petitioner by a registered sale deed being No. 478 dated 8-1-1985 and on delivering possession in his favour, became completely extinguished there from, and after purchase, while the petitioner started enjoying and possessing the land in question peacefully within the knowledge of all, on 1-3-2009, he went to the office of the concerned Assistant Commissioner (Land) for mutation but he came to learn that the land in question has been enlisted as an abandoned property vide the impugned Gazette Notification for which neither he nor his transferor Anwara Ahammed Chowdhury was given any notice. 

 4. Mr Moudud Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the impugned enlistment of the land in question is in violative of the principles of natural justice in view of the fact that neither any prior notice for the said enlistment nor any subsequent notice either for surrender or for taking over possession has been served upon the petitioner or his transferor and, as such, the same is illegal and is liable to be declared to have been done without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. He next submits that the title deeds of the petitioner and his transfer-or, rent receipts as well as the latest record of rights prepared in their names and other connected papers and documents necessarily imply that the petitioner and his transferor always occupied, supervised and managed the land in question in person and, as such, the impugned enlistment is illegal. Lastly the learned Advocate submits that both the petitioner and his transferor are the citizens of Bangladesh as they were born in Bangladesh and they were always present in Bangladesh and their whereabouts were never unknown and they never ceased to occupy, supervise or manage the property in person deserting the same before the commencement of PO No. 16 of 1972 and as the land in question does not fall within the purview of PO No. 16 of 1972, the impugned enlistment being illegal is liable to be declared to have been done without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 6. We have heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner and the learned Deputy Attorney-General representing respondent No.4 and perused the Writ Petition along with other materials on record. 

 14. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The inclusion of the property of the petitioner to the extent of his share measuring 12 decimals of BS Plot No. 157 appertaining to BS Khatian No.9 recorded in the name of the predecessor of the petitioner/ transferor corresponding to PS Plot No.99 of PS Khatian No.52 transformed from RS Plot No.87/104 as appearing in item No.98 mentioning Plot No.9, Mouza-Pahartali under PS Double Mooring at page-15656(Kha) published in the Bangladesh Gazette on 26-12-1988 vide SRO No.378-Law dated 25-12-1988 purportedly made under section 5(1) of the Bangladesh Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance 1985 (Annexure-B to the petition) are declared to have been made without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect and respondent No. 1 is directed to exclude the property in question from the said Gazette notification dated 26-12-1988.

The definite caseof the defendant is that the recorded owners namely Annayda Charan Das and others settled the suit land to the defendant on 5th Baishak, 1350 BS and inducted her into possession.
