5. At the trial, the contesting defendants and the other defendants, who prayed for saham, adduced evidence, both oral and documentary, in support of their respective cases? The trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record by judgment and decree dated 10.01.2005 decreed the suit on contest against defendant Nos.l-5, 7-9, 15-19, 20, 21 and 23-26 and ex-parte against the other defendants giving saham to the plaintiffs to the extent of 1.27 acres of land declaring their title therein and also giving direction upon the defendants to deliver possession of the said land to the plaintiffs. The trial Court also gave saham to defendant Nos.l-5, 7- 9, 15-19 and 20, 21 and 23-26 to the extent of 90 acre, 1.09 acres, 1.75 acres and 69 acre respectively.. The trial Court directed the parties to partition the suit land as per the saham amicably within 60 days from the date of drawing the decree failing which they would get the saham through Court. 

 7. From the pleadings of the contesting parties, the prayer for saham of the defendants as stated hereinbefore and from the judgment and decree of two Courts below, it appears that the main controversy in the suit was as to the claim of defendant Nos.l-5 in respect of 66 acre and 62 acre of land which were allegedly purchased by defendant No.1 by two kabalas being No.5362 dated 10.04.1967 and No.2143 dated 08.02.1965 marked as exhibits-'Ka' and 'KW. From the judgment and decree of the trial Court, it appears that it did not accept the said case of defendant Nos. 1-5 as to their claim to 28 acres of land on the specific finding that the kabalas by which they claimed to have purchased those area of land were created, fictitious and ineffective (in Bengali it has been written as বিবাদী পক্ষের ৮/৩/৬৫ ইং ও ১০/০৪/৬৭ ইং তারিখের কবলা দুখানা শৃষ্ট, ভূয়া ও অকাযকর দলিল). The Appellate Court, though the last Court of fact, did not, at all, reverse the said finding of the trial Court and not only that it did not, at all, consider the case of the plaintiffs that the said two deeds were created by defendant No.1 taking the advantage of the fact that the Sub-registry Office of Palashbari was burnt during the liberation war and the evidence on record in that respect. 'The Appellate Court accepted the said two deeds (exhibits-'Ka' and `Kha') on their face value and gave defendant Nos. 1-5 saham to the extent of 2.18 acres. The trial Court further found that the deeds (exhibits-'Ka' and `Kha') were not acted upon and the record of rights were not prepared in the name of the predecessor of defendant Nos. 1-5 and they did not pay any rent, lax etc. in respect of the said land. The trial Court further found that no permission was obtained from the Sub-Divisional Officer for registration of the deeds which was mandatory at the relevant time, the vendors being. Hindu, the Appellate Court considered nothing. It is also necessary to keep on record that the Appellate Court found saham given by the trial Court to the plaintiffs and the other defendants correct. 

 8. The High Court Division, as it appears from the impugned judgment and order, on consideration of the evidence on record, oral and documentary, found the findings arrived at by the trial Court correct and accordingly, set aside the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court I and restored those of the trial Court. 

 9.  3. The plaint case in short, was that an area measuring 49 decimals of land appertaining to mouza Gaoail, C.S. Khatian No. 23, plot No. 1054 corresponding to R.S. plot No.1054 and 2033 originally belonged to Alokeshi Bewa and her name was correctly recorded in the C.S. Khatian. Alokeshi Bewa died leaving behind her brother-in-law's son Surendra Mohan Sarkar. While Surendra Mohan Sarkar was in possession of the said land as the rightful owner he sold 27 decimals of land from plot No.1054 to Sheikh Jobed Ali and Sree Roy Chand Sutradhar vide kabala dated 12.05.1951 being No. 2440. Subsequently, Surendra Mohan Sarkar purchased 7812 decimals of land including 27 decimals of land of plot No.1054 from Sheikh Jobed Ali and Sree Roy Chandra Sutradhar through deed dated 01.11.1957 being No.7794, but the record was wrongly prepared in the name of Sree Roy Chand Sutradhar in S.A. Khatian Nos.77, 78 and 391. Surendra Mohan Sarkar died leaving behind two sons Haridash Sarkar and Ruhidas Sarkar and while they were in possession of the suit land they sold 20 decimals of land to plaintiff No.1 vide kabala dated 12.06.1997 being No. 4449. Haridash also sold 1312 decimals of land to plaintiff  No.1 vide kabala dated 19.07.1998 being No. 6467. Defendant Nos.1 and 2 have created a collusive deed on 04.12.1998 in respect of 13 decimals of land showing defendant No.1 as the reversioner heir of S.A. recorded tenant Sree Roy Chand Sutradhar which is false and concocted. The deed dated 04.12.1979 was not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

 5. In the written statement filed by defendant Nos. 1 and 2 they contended, inter-alia that the suit land originally belonged to Alokeshi Bewa who died leaving behind Surendra Mohan Sarkar as her heir. Surendra Mohan Sarkar sold 27 decimals of land to Sheikh Jobed Ali and Roy Chand Sutradhar vide kabala dated 12.05.1951. Thereafter, Sheikh Jobed Ali sold his  share in the suit land to Roy Chand and accordingly, S.A. record was correctly prepared in the name of Roy Chand Sutradhar. Roy Chand , Sutradhar died leaving behind 2 sons, namely, Romesh and Gonesh. Romesh and Gonesh transferred 13 decimals of land to defendant No.1 Mohadashi Sutradhar by a deed of gift dated 04.12.19978 and since then defendant No. 1 has been possessing the suit land through her son defendant No.2. The suit was filed by making false statements and as such, the same was liable to be dismissed. 

 9. Mr. Awlad Ali, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioners, has contended that the learned Judge of the High Court Division failed to consider that the appellate Court without adverting to the finding of the trial Court that Ruhidash and Haridash, the vendors of the plaintiffs had not been in possession of the suit land prior to the transfer to them and thus, the plaintiffs have no possession ins the suit land and consequently, the suit was barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and thus, fell into an error in passing the impugned judgment and order affirming those of the appellate Court. Mr. Awlad Ali has further contended that the possession being one of the most important process for elucidation of fact of a case which the trial Court found in favour of the defendant after considering the evidence on record, both in examination-in-chief and in cross-examination, the learned Judge of the High Court Division without considering the evidence of the P.W.s particularly in cross-examination affirmed those of the appellate Court and thus erred in law in passing the impugned judgment and order and as such, the same calls for interference by this Court by way of granting leave. 

 10. From the impugned judgment, it appears that the High Court Division considered the evidence on record and then came to the finding to the effect; 

 "On consideration of the evidence and materials on record it appears that all the P.W's categorically have stated that Haridash and Ruhidash two sons of Surendra permanently lived in this country and only 1⁄2 years hack they left this country. So, the defendants totally failed to establish that the deeds of the plaintiffs Ext.6 and 7 were not executed and registered by the sons of Surrendra Mohan Sarkar." 

 11. It further appears that the High Court Division also found that the trial Court Misread the evidence and materials on record and illegally held that the plaintiffs have not acquired title, interest and possession in the suit land. It further appears that the High Court Division noticed that all the P.W.s stated that the defendants have no possession in the suit land. The High Court Division further noticed that the appellate Court on consideration of the entire evidence of P.W.'s and D.W.'s came to the finding that plaintiffs are in possession in the suit land and that the defendants have no right, title, interest and possession therein. 

 12. It is by now a well settled principle of law that the appellate Court is the last Court of fact. We have gone through the judgment of the appellate Court from which it appears that the appellate Court while arriving at the finding of possession of the plaintiff in the suit land considered all the evidence on record both oral and documentary. The appellate Court also found that the defendants vendors, name Romesh and Ganesh, sons of Roy Chandra Sutradhar had no right, title and possession over the suit land and so they had no right to transfer the same to them. Mr. Awlad Ali has failed to show before us with reference to any particular evidence which the appellate Court misread or did not consider in arriving at the above findings of fact which if considered the conclusions would have been otherwise.

Dag Nos. 7, 110 and 113 and the bill for compensation for acquiring the land had been made in the names of the plaintiffs 

 4. Mr. Md. Abu Siddique, learned Advocate-on-Weird, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division passed the impugned judgment and order giving complete relief to the defendants before giving an opportunity to the plaintiffs to put their case; that the defendants suppressed the whole material facts and the High Court Division failed to apply its judicial mind in assessing the materials on record and the provision of law applicable thereto that the High Court Division manifestly erred in law resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice in misreading the evidence on record and failed to consider the legal and admitted facts and in basing decision on mere surmise and conjecture. The learned Advocate-on-Record further submitted that the High Court Division illegally disturbed the concurrent Finding of fact while the Courts of below on proper reading of the evidence of the contesting parties and on a careful consideration, meticulous analysis and exploration of the evidence on record found that the plaintiffs having been proved their title on the suit land, thus the Courts below have com-mitted no error of law resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice and as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. 

 5. It appears that the plaintiffs filed a suit for declaration of title and also for declaration that the record of S.A. Khatian in the name of Ausha Miah is wrong. The trial Court decreed the suit land and on appeal, the Court of Appeal below affirmed the judgment and decree of The trial COURT It appears that Rajabdi died leaving by Bangu Sheik and Atabdi as his two sons to inherit the properties left behind him and Bangu Sheikh died leaving behind his wife Rupban and three daughters Joynab, Payrun Nessa and Maju Bibi. It appears that Aushi Bibi wife of Kalimuddin, Manaf and Alam sons of Kalimuddin transferred their shares in favour of Ausha Miah in the year, 1937 by exhibit-Gl. The plaintiff claimed that Bangu Sheikh while alive, by way of oral gift handed over the property in question in favour of the wife of his grand son, Aushi Bibi. It further appears that one Aushi was in possession and in subsequent S.A. Khatian and R.S. Khatian it was shown that Ausha Miah was in possession of the suit land. The plaintiff claimed the title of the property in question on the basis of an oral gift given by Bangu Sheikh in appears that the documents as exhibited by the defendants especially the Heba deed in favour of Ausha Miah, sale deeds, the decree of partition suit etc. being documentary evidence were not discussed by the Courts below. The oral Heba in favour of Aushi Bibi could not be proved by any evidence. Therefore, oral or extraneous evidence to contradict the terms of the contents of a document is inadmissible under Section 92 of the Evidence Act. It appears that record of right is evidence of present possession and a registered kabala is an evidence of gift. In the instant case, Aushi Bibi though claimed the property by way of oral gift she could not prove the oral gift by adducing any evidence. There is nothing on record to show that she has title on the property but on the other hand, the title of the property passed on Ausha Miah by three registered documents, one is the Heba deed and two others by registered sale deeds. 

 6. The High Court Division observed that the plaintiffs failed to prove their title on the suit land and the fact that the name of Ausha Miah was recorded wrongly in the C.S. Khatian and subsequent S.A. and R.S. Khatians. Unless and until the registered deeds in favour of Ausha Miah and the C.S. and R.S. Khatians in his name are cancelled by a competent Court or by competent Authority, the plaintiff's claims will remain an illusion. The Courts below did not at all discuss the documentary evidence as exhibited by the defendants, as discussed by the High Court Division, which were admitted by the Court below without any objection. It is a clear case where the Courts below have committed an error of law resulting in an erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice, the High Court Division under its revisional jurisdiction is inclined to interfere with the concur-rent findings of the Courts below.

 3.  7. It appears from the record that this property was purchased by one Abdur Rahman in the year 1962 and since then he had been living there with his family members by mutating his name in the record of rights and paying rents of the house to the authorities. But during the war of liberation Abdur Rahman was absent in the premises and his whereabouts where not known at the relevant time i.e. on 28-2-1972 and accordingly the property was duly declared as abandoned property and vested as an abandoned property under PO No. 16 of 1972. It is the case of the Government that after liberation nobody possessed the premises which remained a vacant as the abandoned property. But the present respondent somehow managed to trespass into possession on the basis of a procured sale deed. Finding an unauthorized person possessing the premises the Government issued a notice to surrender possession of the property and ousted the respondent from the house and took over possession in the year 1976. Thereafter, the Authority leased out the premises to a leasee who is now in possession now. These defendants have been in possession of 0.11 decimals of land out of a22 decimals of land from plot No. 545; Karim Mollah, Fazal Mollah and Nehal Uddin were the owner the owners of plot No. 554 and 555. Nehal uddin used to possess 16 annas share of plot No. 551 and 553 as homestead. Nehal Uddin Mollah also used to possess 0.46 decimals of land from plot No. 554. Karim Mollah and those defendants used to possess 0.57 decimals of land from plot No. 554 Afazuddin got 0.32 decimals of land from plot No. 1712 by amicable exchange with plot No. 844 and 854 with these defendants and transferred those lands to one Liakat Ali. The title deeds of the plaintiffs are false, collusive and the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 5. Mr. A.K.M Shafiqul Alam, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the High Court Division due to misconception of law as well as facts passed the impugned judgment and order it which is liable to be set aside in the interest of justice; that the plaintiff herein petitioners   claimed the suit land as their ancestral properties as well as vide some Registered and settlement deeds which clearly exhibited and proved by the plaintiff   by giving proper evidence; that after perusing the deeds filed by the plaintiff it is crystal clear that by way of 5 Registered deeds the plaintiffs herein petitioners have been possessing 1.47 chhataks of lands, that in the part of the suit land, there is a homestead of the plaintiffs situated in the scheduled-B which was even not denied by the defendant-respondents herein; that the plaintiff have been able to prove its case by giving all the necessary documentary evidence which were duly exhibited before the Court; that the defendants did not deny at all in the written statements as well as in deposition that the suit land is paternal properties and also could not be able to prove the alleged deeds as false, forged and fabricated as well; actually all the deeds filed by the plaintiffs were genuine, and accordingly proved by the plaintiff before the Court; that the plaintiff herein petitioners got every right, title, interest and possession over the suit land; that the defendant respondents herein could not be able to prove that in any manner that they have been enjoying the suit land, which is clearly evident in the Case Records; that the defendants in their deposition clearly acknowledged the title and possession of the suit land by the plaintiffs; that it has also been proved that the plaintiffs have been enjoying some properties as ejmali properties and some properties as their purchased properties vide some registered deeds. 

 6. It appears from the record that plaintiff No.1 examined himself as only witness and in support of his case he filed the amolnama, kabala and Khatian. On the side of the defendants they examined 3 witnesses and produced bainanama, two kabala deeds, one DCR, a number of Khatians and a number of rent receipts in support of their case. It is the plaint case that they got the suit land by purchase through amolnama by gift and inheritance. These are modes of acquisition property by a person and it is found that the plaintiffs left no stone unturned in acquiring the suit property. It is the case of plaintiffs that they possess the suit land but the recent record of rights has been wrongly prepared. It is settled principle of law plaintiff is to prove his own case and it is also not denied that number of witnesses is not required to deny the factum one case, From the deposition of P.W.1 it is found that the plaintiffs acquired title by purchase through amolnama, by gift and by inheritance. 

 7. It also appears from the record that plaintiff produced the kabala deeds, exhibited as exhibit-2 to 2(c) and from these deeds it appears that plaintiffs purchased total 1.01 decimals of land. Against this purchase of the plaintiffs defendants made 7 out a case that they have got the Suit land from the person who purchased the aforesaid land in execution on a money decree. Defendants did not produce any writ of delivery showing they have got possession 7 pursuant to the said money decree. But it has been found that plaintiff did not produced   any rent receipts to show they are actually in possession of the suit land. Coupled with this fact that admitted possession and the recent record of right it is very heard to consume that the plaintiffs have been processing the land by purchase of the suit land in 1947 moreso, it is curious enough that they did not even file any rent receipts or adduce any witness, save and except P.W.1 to prove they ever entered into possession of the suit land. Moreover, the plaintiffs did not adduce any evidence to show that in their deeds of 1947 the suit land was wrongly written as dag No. 845 instead of dag No. 854.

2. Facts necessary for disposal of the Rule are that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 153 of 1988 praying for a declaration of title in the suit land as described in Ka schedule land to the plaint. That suit was transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Barisal and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 36 of 1994. The plaint's case was, inter alia, that the Ka schedule land belonged to Hamejuddin and others. Hatem Ali died leaving behind two daughters Garibjan Bibi and Fatejan Bibi and a son Aptar Ali. The suit land was diluviated into the river in the year, 1934 and reappeared after 15 years i.e. before the Part V of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came into being. The revisional survey took place in the year, 1940-42 and, as a result, the RS Khatians were published showing the property to be diluviated. Hamejuddin and Sadat Ali sold their entire share on 12-5-66 in favour of the petitioner Nos. 1-2 and 5-6 and Aptar sold his share to petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 on 5-10-56. Recorded tenant Aminuddin sold his share to petitioner Nos. 1, 2 and 4 on 24-2-68 and delivered possession thereof. Aptar Ali and Garibjan sold their share on 25-5-68 to petitioner Nos. 1-3. This way the petitioners have been in possession in the suit land by constructing their homestead. The defendant opposite parties had no title and possession in the suit land who taking advantage of a note in the record of rights as diluviated land; the concerned Tahshilder claimed the suit property by the first week of Polish 1395 BS and, as such, the suit. 

 6. Upon consideration of the evidence on record, the trial Court dismissed the suit by the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-8-1995 against which the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 165 of 1995. The said appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Barisal who by the impugned judgment and decree dated 27-6-2000 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment of the trial Court. 

 9. Mr Md Ferozur Rahman, the learned Assistant Attorney-General, on appearing for the opposite parties, submitted that the property was under water. He submitted that the evidence on record supported that the suit property came within the mischief of President's Order No. 135 of 1972. He further submitted that the Courts below upon consideration of the evidence on record lawfully dismissed the plaintiffs' suit. He further submitted that the plaintiffs, in the revisional application, could not make out any case of non-consideration of any evidence or non-reading of any evidence or misreading of any evidence on record and finally, submitted that there is nothing to interfere by this Court in revision against the concurrent finding of facts arrived at by both the Courts below. 

 11. On perusal of the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court it appears that the plaintiff has sought for declaration of title in a part of a number of plots without specifying the area. The trial Court upon consideration of the evidence on record found the plaintiffs to be out of possession and the appellate Court affirmed the said finding. Mr Swapan Kumar Dutta could not point out from the evidence on record that any evidence is available to support the plaintiffs' possession in the suit. Moreover, the suit land having not been specified and having not been abutted and bounded, a suit for declaration of title is barred under the proviso of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and also under Order VII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Mr Md Firozur Rahman, the learned Assistant Attorney-General relied upon two decisions of our Appellate Division reported in 41 DLR (AD) 141 and / BLC (AD) 26. The further case of the defendant petitioner was that Subrata and Shubendu sons of Suresh Chowdhury contracted to sell Dag No. 2283 of the 2nd schedule land with defendant Nos. 1 and 2 on 10.04.1964 and delivered possession thereof. That the defendant took settlement in 1358 B.S. of the suit 3rd scheduled land from the zamindar Romesh Chandra Chowdhury and Suresh Chandra Chowdhury and since then was possessing the same as residence and living there with their family. That as the record of right wrongly prepared in the name of Ex-land Lord, this defendant filed Title Suit No. 150 of 1969 in the first court of Munsif Sylhet for correction of the record of rights; that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 202 of 19769 was not binding upon this defendant as he was not a party to the suit and that the plaintiff had no right title or interest over the suit land and hence prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 7. Mr. M. A. Samid with, Mr. M.G.H. Ruhullah, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties submitted that both the courts below acted legally and com-mitted no mistake in passing their judgments and decrees. He further argued that the trial court rightly observed that Suresh had only one son which was evident from the fact that the defendant in Title Suit No. 150 of 1969 for correction of record of right made Subrata Chowdhury son of late Suresh Chowdhury as defendant No. 2 and none else and this clearly showed that Suresh had only one son and it also got strength from the certified copy of the petition filed by defendant in Title Execution Case No. 5 of 1970. In the said petition Sunkar was admitted by the defendant as only son of Suresh and from this evidence it was clear that Suresh had only one son namely Sankar and not Subrata. He also submitted that the lower appellate court had rightly observed that Ext.-C হইতেছে দেওয়ানী ১৫০/১৯৬৯ নং মোকদ্দমার ডিক্রীর সই মুহুরী নকল। উক্ত দেওয়ানী ১৫০/১৯৬৯ নং মোকদ্দমাটি বাদী ইন্তাজ আলী দায়ের করেন রেকর্ড সংশোধনের মোকদ্দমা এবং উক্ত মোকদ্দমার ২নং বিবাদী হিসাবে সুব্রত চন্দ্র চৌধুরী পিল মৃত সুরেশ চন্দ্র চৌধুরীকে একমাত্র ছেলে হিসাবে দেখানো হয়েছে। পি.ডব্লিউ-১ অঞ্জন খা তাহার জবান বন্দীতে বলেন ১৪নং বিবাদী শংকর প্রসাদ চৌধুরী সুরেশ চন্দ্র এর একমাত্র ছেলে। --------   and on this score the lower appellate court had observed that though the defendant No. 1, dismissed the decree of the Title Suit No. 202 of 1969 and also Title Execution No. 5 of 1970 but the defendant did not file any suit challenging the legality of Title Suit No. 202 of 1969 and Title execution Case No. 5 of 1970 and as such the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial court in Title Suit No. 202 of 1969 was valid in the eye of law. He finally argued that the petitioner never was in possession of the suit property since he neither mentioned his possession any where in written statement or memo appeal or Revisional application. In support of his argument he referred the cases of Zamir Uddin Ahmed Vs. Ziaul Huq and others, reported in 49 DLR622 and Md. Shah Alam Vs. Musammat Panda Begum, reported in 17BLD(AD)145. 

 8. I have perused the materials on record and it is found that both the courts below elaborately have considered all the aspects of the case. The Courts below categorically discussed the evidence on record of both the sides and other materials in passing their judgments and decrees. I have also observed the referred decisions and the way the courts below made observation on evidence and other materials on record which in my opinion both the courts below committed no error of law. In the situation this case has no merit and nothing to interfere with the judgments and decrees of the courts below. 

 Lower courts record be sent down at once.

The aforesaid land was recorded as khatian No. 78 and 103 Mohabbatpur Mouza. The other lands of khatian No. 78 were in the name of the father of the plaintiffs and brother Nazir Ahmed. This Munsur Ahmed died leaving behind plaintiffs No. 1, 2 and 3 Nazir Ahmed Anwar Ahmed and Abul Hossain, Nazir Ahmed sold his share to plaintiff No. 1 and Anwar Ahmed and Abul Hossain sold their shares to plaintiff No. 4 in Diara settlement when the name of Munsur Ahmed was not recorded in the record of rights, he filed the suit in the court of Assistant Judge, Sadar Upzilla vide Title Suit No. 23 of 1972. In the above suit the predecessor of the defendant No. 2 to 14 namely Abdul Hye and Solaiman filed written statement from where it appears that Ibrahim Miah filed a suit being Title Suit No. 13 of 1964 challenging he auction purchase of Ataul Haque Chowdhury and got a decree of 63 decimals of land khatian No. 93 in the aforesaid suit. He also got 22 decimals of land of khatian no. 133 on the basis of the decretal cost of the aforesaid Civil Suit and decree execution case the plaintiff got 63 decimals and 22 decimals in total 85 decimals of land but they abandoned their claim of 85 decimals of land and got from Serajul Haque Muktair 1.26 acres of land from Khatian No. 95,96,97 and 99. The names of some other persons were recorded in khatian No. 78 and defendant No. 48 to 52 created some documents and by virtue of that they dispossessed the plaintiff from 'Ka' schedule property in 1985. The lands as contained in the schedules were never partitioned among the co-sharers so, for recovery of `Kha' schedule land for partition of 'Ka' schedule land the plaintiffs instituted the present suit. 

 6. Defendants No. 47 to 49 filed separate written statement stating that the original owner Abul Khair Mohammad Mostafa Haider Chowdhury obtained a rent decree in Rent Suit No. 1760 of 1958 against the recording of the khatian No. 293 and in pursuance of Rent Execution Case No. 110 of 1959, 2.06 acres of land of khatian No. 92 were sold in auction and purchased by Abduyl Hye and Solaiman and got possession of the same through court. Against the aforesaid rent decree Abdul Kader and others, the sons of Serajul Haque Muktair instituted Title Suit No. 254 of 1959 which was dismissed on 12.12.195. These defendants denied right and title of the plaintiff. 

 7. Considering the materials on record of the parties the trial court dismissed the suit of the plaintiffs. Against the judgment and decree of the Trial Court the plaintiff preferred appeal wherein the lower appellate court set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff and the lower Appellate Court declared title of the plaintiff in `Kha' Schedule land and directed for recovery of khas possession and also declared title in 'Ka' schedule land and directed for partition of the same as per prayer made in the plaint. 

 9. Mr. Syed Ziaul Karim, the learned Advocate, appearing for the appellant, having placed before us the impugned judgment of the High Court Division as well as the other materials on record contended firstly that the High Court Division is competent to interfere with the findings of fact if those are based on non-reading and misreading of material evidence on record and also could interfere for misinterpreting exhibit-5 the deed of executed by Ataul Haque Chowdhury in favour of the plaintiff-predecessor Mansur Ahmed and this having being not done, the High Court Division committed an error of law which resulted in an error causing failure of justice. 

 10. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Counsel appearing for the respondents, on the other hand, contended that having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of the materials on record the learned Single Judge having applied his judicial mind rightly decided the case finding no error apparent on the face of judgment of the lower appellate court who as a final court of fact reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court upon proper consideration and assessment of the material evidence on record and in such view of the matter the high Court Division committed no illegality in affirming the judgment of the lower appellate courts as a final court of fact. 

 11. It is further contended that there is no misreading or non-consideration of the material evidence on record by the appellate court who reversed the decision of the trial court and as such the judgment of the High Court Division calls for no interference. 

 13. We have read the impugned judgment of the High Court Division as well as the judgment of the lower Courts below. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, we find that the learned Single Judge having applied his judicial mind in the exercise of revisional jurisdiction rightly found that the lower appellate Court noticed materials on record and thereafter came to the finding in favour of the plaintiff-respondent in decreeing the suit.
